item.content:encoded:
Seattle, Washington.- Cam Schlittler lanzó un juego sin permitir carreras hasta la séptima entrada y Paul Goldschmidt conectó un jonrón de tres carreras, lo que permitió a los Yankees de Nueva York vencer a los Marineros de Seattle por 5-3 el miércoles.
Ben Rice también conectó un jonrón y un doble productor para los Yankees, que terminaron con un récord de 5-1 en su gira por la Costa Oeste al inicio de la temporada. Jugarán su primer partido en casa el viernes contra los Miami Marlins.
Schlittler (2-0) permitió dos hits en 6 1/3 entradas y retiró a sus últimos 16 bateadores, extendiendo su inicio de temporada sin permitir carreras. Ponchó a siete y no otorgó bases por bolas en 79 lanzamientos, 58 de ellos strikes.
El lanzador derecho de 25 años dejó a los Giants sin carreras durante 5 1/3 entradas el viernes pasado. Solo ha permitido tres hits esta temporada, mientras que ha ponchado a 15 bateadores. Tanto él como su compañero Max Fried no han permitido carreras en sus dos aperturas esta temporada.
Brendan Donovan abrió la parte baja de la primera entrada con un doble, pero fue el único jugador que llegó a segunda base contra Schlittler.
David Bednar necesitó 40 lanzamientos para conseguir los cuatro outs y lograr su tercer salvamento.
Nueva York tomó la delantera en la primera entrada con un doble productor de Rice, y Goldschmidt conectó un jonrón contra el abridor George Kirby (1-1) en la sexta entrada, su primer jonrón de la temporada. Fue el primer jonrón de Goldschmidt contra un lanzador diestro desde el 6 de junio.
Rice añadió un jonrón solitario en la novena entrada, su primer jonrón del año.
Cal Raleigh impulsó dos carreras para Seattle con un sencillo de bate roto ante Bednar con dos outs en la octava entrada, reduciendo la desventaja a 4-2. Dominic Canzone conectó un sencillo productor de carrera en la novena entrada.
Desde el partido del lunes por la noche, los lanzadores abridores de los Yankees no han permitido ninguna carrera en 16 entradas consecutivas.
A continuación
El lanzador derecho de los Yankees, Will Warren (0-0), abrirá el viernes contra el lanzador derecho de los Marlins, Eury Pérez (0-0).
El lanzador derecho de los Mariners, Bryan Woo (0-0), recibirá la pelota el viernes por la noche como visitante contra el lanzador zurdo de los Angels de Los Ángeles, Reid Detmers (0-0).
Información: AP.

item.description: Pavin Smith's pinch-hit, walk-off homer lifts D-backs over Yankees (Photo credit: Arianna Grainey) Pinch-hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory. item.content:encoded:
Pavin Smith's pinch-hit, walk-off homer lifts D-backs over Yankees
(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch-hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 389-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the AL East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
The D-backs (81-74) gained a game on Philadelphia (85-70) for the third spot in the National League wild-card race but are still four games back with seven games to play.
Yankees starter and American League Cy Young candidate Cam Schlittler gave up three hits and three runs (one earned) in six innings, leaving when his pitch count reached 98. His season high is 106.
Schlittler struck out three and walked six while lowering his ERA to an American League-leading 1.94. He has given up one earned run or fewer in each of his last eight starts.
Arizona starter Brandon Pfaadt gave up four singles and one run in 4 1/3 innings, leaving after the Yankees loaded the bases on three singles in the fifth. Ben Rice hit a sacrifice fly off Justin Martinez to break a scoreless tie. Pfaadt struck out three and walked one.
The D-backs broke up Schlittler's no-hitter with a two-run fifth. Both runs scored after Schlittler's one-out fielding error.
Arenado had Arizona's first hit, a line single to left field with one out, before Tim Tawa pushed a bunt toward the mound. Schlittler could not field the ball cleanly and both runners were safe.
Lawlar lined a two-out triple to left-center on a 99 mph fastball for a 2-1 lead.
Ramos and Wells homered in the sixth to put the Yankees in front 3-2.
The D-backs tied it in the sixth when Ketel Marte and Gabriel Moreno drew four-pitch walks and Geraldo Perdomo beat out a two-strike bunt single to load the bases. Corbin Carroll hit a sacrifice fly before Schlittler struck out Arenado and Tawa with runners on second and third.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [fingerlakes1.com] Yankees let lead slip away in walk-off loss to Diamondbacks | Fingerlakes1.com
item.dc:creator: Facebook Com; Fingerlakes1; Kyle Evans
item.description: The New York Yankees suffered a tough loss on Saturday night, falling to the Arizona Diamondbacks 5-3 on Pavin Smith’s two-run walk-off home run in the ninth inning. The loss came after the Yankees twice held a lead earlier in the game. New York broke through in the fifth inning when Austin Wells, Anthony Volpe and José Caballero opened the frame with consecutive singles to load the bases. Ben Rice followed with a sacrifice fly that brought home Wells and put the Yankees ahead 1-0. Arizona answe
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees suffered a tough loss on Saturday night, falling to the Arizona Diamondbacks 5-3 on Pavin Smith’s two-run walk-off home run in the ninth inning.
The loss came after the Yankees twice held a lead earlier in the game. New York broke through in the fifth inning when Austin Wells, Anthony Volpe and José Caballero opened the frame with consecutive singles to load the bases. Ben Rice followed with a sacrifice fly that brought home Wells and put the Yankees ahead 1-0.
Arizona answered in the bottom half of the inning, taking a 2-1 lead on Jordan Lawler’s two-run triple. Both runs were unearned against Yankees starter Cam Schlittler, who committed a fielding error on a sacrifice bunt during the inning.
New York responded quickly in the sixth. Heliot Ramos tied the game with a solo home run before Wells put the Yankees back in front with his 13th home run of the season. Both home runs came against Arizona reliever Kevin Ginkel.
Schlittler ran into trouble again in the bottom of the sixth after issuing two walks and allowing a single to load the bases with nobody out. Corbin Carroll tied the game with a sacrifice fly, but Schlittler struck out the next two batters to escape further damage.
Schlittler completed six innings, allowing three runs on three hits with three walks and six strikeouts over 98 pitches. Only one of the three runs was earned, and his season earned-run average dropped to 1.94.
Neither team scored again until the ninth, when Smith ended the game with his two-run homer off Michael Fulmer.
The Yankees will finish the series Sunday at 4:10 p.m. Will Warren will face Corbin Burnes.

item.content:encoded:
One would figure that with Cam Schlittler going on Saturday night, this would be the game for the Yankees to win if they had any hope for a last-ditch AL East comeback, but something about Arizona wore down the likely Cy Young Award winner tonight. The Snakes were pesky, annoying, and other terms my editors won’t let me use while in the batter’s box tonight, finally breaking through on a Pavin Smith walk-off home run, to win it, 5-3.
Right off the top, I need to be grumpy about something. Nobody likes West Coast games and nobody likes the fact that every time the Yankees are on the West Coast, they play more night games than day games. This goes double for West Coast Yankee fans, because the beautiful thing about cheering for an East Coast team is they start playing when you get off work, or when you’re just finishing your Saturday morning coffee, the game takes three hours and you have the evening to yourself. That doesn’t happen on these trips.
Now, the Diamondbacks were celebrating the only World Series title in history, 25 years ago this season. I get it, you want to have a special event, the team isn’t very good so the end of the season starts to drag a little bit, you want a little spice. I even respect the cheek of waiting until the Yankees are in town. What I don’t respect is being completely incapable of running a functioning ceremony. The Yankees have Old Timer’s Day every year, they designate a special start time and at that time, the festivities have concluded and we can get down to the reason we’re all here, to watch a baseball game, which I don’t think is an unreasonable expectation at a baseball stadium with a baseball team in town.
The Diamondbacks started their pregame ceremonies at 4:30pm local time, with a scheduled 5:10pm first pitch. They absolutely blew past that in a way that, in my opinion, was both unprofessional and downright insulting. The four clocks I have ready access to in my apartment agreed: Brandon Pfaadt didn’t throw his first offering to Ben Rice until 5:42pm. This was an absolute joke of a start to the series’ second game. That all this happened in a city I’m predisposed to dislike already was…whatever the anti-cherry on top. I also firmly don’t like the existence of Phoenix as a city in general so I was always going to be ticked off watching this one.
I said in the gamethread that we had maybe begun to develop outsized expectations for Cam Schlittler. He’s been SO good, for long enough, that we needed to remember the other team all drives nice cars and lives in nice houses too. While Cam did get through 4.1 innings without allowing a hit, the Diamondbacks pushed a pair of runs across in the fifth. Nolan Arenado reached with a one-out single, before Tim Tawa attempted to give himself up with a sac bunt. Schlittler couldn’t corral what should have been an out though, an error that put two men on, and #9 hitter Jordan Lawlar made him pay:
Funny enough, because Schlittler was charged with that error, both of the runs were unearned, and he still hasn’t allowed more than a single earned run in eight starts now. The Yankees would tie the game the next inning, but all those extra pitches taxed his right arm, and I think had a major impact on what would happen in the sixth.
Speaking of tying the game, Heliot Ramos was brought to New York because of his opposite field power. He stunk in his first taste of East Coast baseball, but has looked much more representative in his last 20 games, and flexed that oppo pop within moments of Schlittler getting back in the dugout:
Corbin Carroll ran down a sinking Anthony Volpe liner for the second out, a very nice play that loomed larger when Austin Wells stepped to the plate:
Wells is getting hot at the right time, with three home runs in his last five games and he’s actually been a league average hitter since August 1! The nice thing about being a good defensive catcher is if you can just not embarrass yourself at the plate, you’re a major asset for your team.
The good vibes only lasted until Cam got back on the mound though. I think the error and the triple shook him up a little, and we’ve seen this happen before. Schlittler’s a high-energy guy, when that energy is less than positive I do think he gets a little in his own head and starts to overthrow. He walked the first two batters of the inning on eight total pitches, completely uncompetitive at-bats that are just so out of whack with what he’s done so far this season.
A soft Geraldo Perdomo bunt loaded the bases, and Cam did seem to lock in at that point. Corbin Carroll did bring in the third Snakes run of the game — and the only earned for Cam — but the ace got both Arenado and Tawa to whiff to end the threat. It was a weird one for Schlittler tonight, but 6.0 IP and one earned run is what the line reads.
The bullpen wasn’t exactly dynamite in Cam’s stead; the Diamondbacks have the third-lowest strikeout rate in baseball and their ability to grind out at-bats showed, even if the Yankees got through eight innings keeping the game tied at three. This was a long, miserable game, and wasn’t helped by the fact the Yankees couldn’t really find the nine-run spark that they showed on Friday.
If nothing else, I got to re-hate Michael Fulmer, and all those feelings from 2016 sprung forth anew. He walked the leadoff batter to open the ninth, and gave up the walk-off dinger to Pavin Smith:
The division race is functionally over with the Rays’ win earlier today, as they restored their five-game lead. Get yourself set for the Wild Card, lock up home-field advantage for that series, and don’t get yourselves hurt. The Yankes finish this series tomorrow with Will Warren on the hill. First pitch is supposedly at 4:10pm Eastern, but we’ll see.

item.content:encoded:
Los New York Yankees respondieron con autoridad en su primer partido sin Aaron Judge y derrotaron 9-2 a los Arizona Diamondbacks este viernes en Chase Field. Nueva York fabricó cinco carreras en la primera entrada, Ben Rice y George Lombard Jr. conectaron cuadrangulares y Gerrit Cole lanzó seis entradas de calidad para llevarse una victoria que también tuvo un significado histórico para el derecho.
LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Aaron Judge vuelve a la lista de lesionados de los Yankees!
LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Dodgers ya son campeones de la División Oeste!
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
La jornada comenzó con una noticia importante para los Yankees: Judge fue colocado nuevamente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha. Sin su principal figura ofensiva, Nueva York necesitó encontrar producción desde el primer turno y la respuesta llegó inmediatamente frente al abridor de Arizona, Eduardo Rodríguez.
Los primeros cinco bateadores de los Yankees lograron embasarse. Ben Rice recibió una base por bolas y posteriormente Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo productor para abrir la pizarra. Después llegaron más oportunidades para la ofensiva neoyorquina, hasta que George Lombard Jr. conectó un sencillo de dos carreras que llevó el marcador a 5-0 antes de que terminara el primer episodio. Rodríguez necesitó 45 lanzamientos para conseguir los tres outs de la entrada, la mayor cantidad de su carrera en un primer inning.
Arizona intentó reaccionar en el segundo capítulo. Corbin Carroll conectó un cuadrangular de dos carreras para acercar a los Diamondbacks a 5-2 y darle algo de vida al público de Chase Field. Sin embargo, Cole logró contener la ofensiva local y evitó que la reacción se transformara en una amenaza mayor.
La respuesta de los Yankees llegó en la tercera entrada. Ben Rice volvió a aparecer y conectó un cuadrangular solitario, su número 39 de la temporada, para recuperar la diferencia de cuatro carreras y colocar el encuentro 6-2. El batazo también completó una noche ofensiva sobresaliente para Rice, quien terminó con dos imparables, dos bases por bolas, dos carreras y dos carreras impulsadas.
Mientras la ofensiva seguía produciendo, Cole encontró estabilidad desde la lomita. Después del cuadrangular de Carroll, el derecho no permitió otra carrera y completó seis entradas con cuatro hits, dos carreras limpias, ninguna base por bolas y seis ponches. Venía de dos aperturas en las que había permitido siete jonrones combinados, por lo que su actuación en Phoenix representó una recuperación importante en su temporada.
Lombard Jr. volvió a aparecer en la sexta entrada. El campocorto conectó su tercer jonrón de la temporada, esta vez solitario, para ampliar la ventaja de Nueva York a 7-2. El joven infielder terminó la noche con dos imparables y tres carreras impulsadas, convirtiéndose en otra de las figuras ofensivas del triunfo visitante.
Ver esta publicación en Instagram
Los Yankees agregaron dos carreras más en la séptima entrada para terminar de sentenciar el encuentro. La ofensiva visitante terminó con ocho hits y nueve carreras, mientras que Arizona consiguió siete imparables, pero no volvió a pisar el plato después del segundo inning.
Para Cole, la victoria tuvo un valor especial. El derecho llegó a 162 triunfos en su carrera, superando a Mike Moore y convirtiéndose en el lanzador con más victorias entre los jugadores que fueron seleccionados con el primer pick global del Draft. Cole fue elegido por los Pittsburgh Pirates con la primera selección en 2011.
La derrota, en cambio, complicó todavía más el panorama de Arizona en la recta final de la temporada. Los Diamondbacks llegaron al encuentro buscando mantenerse en la pelea por el último boleto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, pero la caída ante Nueva York significó su tercera derrota consecutiva. Al término de la jornada quedaron cinco juegos por detrás del último puesto de Wild Card, con ocho encuentros restantes.
Los Yankees, ya clasificados a los playoffs, mejoraron a 89-64 y se colocaron a cuatro juegos de los Tampa Bay Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana, con nueve partidos por disputar. Nueva York además consiguió su octava victoria en sus últimos 10 encuentros.
El triunfo llegó, además, en una noche en la que los Yankees tuvieron que afrontar la ausencia de Judge. Rice y Lombard Jr. aportaron los batazos largos, mientras que Cole respondió desde el montículo para que Nueva York tomara el primer partido de la serie en Arizona con una victoria contundente de 9-2.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees at Diamondbacks. Cam Schlittler dominating in early innings
The Yankees broke through with the first run of the game in the top of the fifth inning, while the Diamondbacks are still looking for their first hit off Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler.
The Diamondbacks trail the Yankees, 1-0, after 4½ innings as play continued at Chase Field on Saturday, Sept. 19.
The Yankees loaded the bases on three singles in the fifth off right-hander Brandon Pfaadt, prompting manager Torey Lovullo to make an aggressive move to his bullpen. Right-hander Justin Martinez entered and recorded two fly-ball outs, the first of which, by Ben Rice, was deep enough to score the first run of the night.
The Diamondbacks are trying to keep their slim playoff hopes alive with a win. Meanwhile, the San Diego Padres, whom the Diamondbacks are hoping to catch, were losing to the Marlins at Petco Park.
The game started about a half-hour late after a lengthy pregame ceremony honoring the Diamondbacks’ 2001 World Series team.
With former radio voice Greg Schulte hosting the ceremony, the Diamondbacks introduced players, coaches and staff from the ‘01 team. Randy Johnson was the last one announced. While everyone else entered the field from beyond the right-field fence, Johnson came out of the home bullpen in left field, a call back to his relief appearance in Game 7 of the World Series.
One of the memorable moments of the pregame ceremony was when trumpeter Dr. Jesse McGuire, performing the national anthem as he did at the World Series in 2001, hit a sour note on his instrument. Then the trumpet gave out completely, and McGuire acted quickly by grabbing the microphone and singing the rest of the Star-Spangled Banner.
Afterward, he received a hug from Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo as the crowd cheered.
—Nick Piercoro and Jose M. Romero
With his team teetering on the brink of elimination, Lovullo’s job status is again a topic of discussion. Lovullo understands. For him, it’s nothing new.
“It seems to be a very important part of the conversation for a lot of people,” Lovullo said on Saturday, Sept. 19, a day after his team lost for the third consecutive day to drop five games out of a playoff spot with eight games remaining.
“For me, it’s real, I understand it, but it’s the realities of this game. You’ve got to win. That’s what it comes down to. Have we won enough? You know, I want to win every game that we play.”
Lovullo, in his 10th season as Diamondbacks manager, has worked as a “lame-duck” manager in four of the past six seasons. He seemed to reference that history, as well as the fact that he had to “fight for everything” during his playing career.
But he said that, for now, at least, he remains focused on doing what he can to help his players and coaches finish out the season.
“When it’s time to worry about it or think about it, whether that’s sooner than later, I will,” he said. “I’ve got to do my job. If I'm worried about different things that I can’t control, then I'm not doing my job for that group in there. I’m doing fine. I’m doing fine. Because I've lived in this space for a long time. I understand the playbook. I understand the realities of this game.”
Last year, Lovullo went into the final weekend of the year with similar questions surrounding him. He found out a day after the season ended that he would be coming back for another year.
The situation is believed to be similar to then: Lovullo has strong support from the baseball operations department and general manager Mike Hazen, but how he is viewed by ownership is less certain.
Lovullo has two postseason appearances — 2017 and 2023 — during his managerial tenure, but he also has presided over multiple late-season collapses. If this year's team continues to stumble, it would mark a third consecutive year the Diamondbacks fell short in September.
Hazen is working under the five-year extension he signed in September 2023. His deal runs through 2028.
The Diamondbacks entered Saturday, Sept. 19, facing long odds at a postseason berth. FanGraphs put their chances at claiming a wild-card spot at about 5%.
—Nick Piecoro
Justin Martinez leaves impression on manager
Members of the 2001 Diamondbacks World Series team milled about in front of the home dugout at Chase Field on Friday, Sept. 18, catching up, taking photos and conducting interviews.
Justin Martinez walked among them, asking each one he approached to sign a baseball. The Diamondbacks reliever later put the ball in a case he had with him in the team clubhouse.
Lovullo said Martinez seeking autographs of veterans is a throwback to a previous generation of players.
“I love it,” Lovullo said. “There was probably seven fistfights between those teammates, firstfights don’t happen anymore. It’s just a different level of camaraderie. But players care about the same thing, and that’s to win the world championship.
“So ‘J-Mart’ was probably just getting a feel for the common denominator based on what drove that team, and that’s a brotherhood that you can’t replace.”
Lovullo added that he's happy that the current team has players that are fans of baseball on that level.
“That he gets to touch their emotions makes it even better. That’s vintage J-Mart," Lovullo said.
— José M. Romero
Yankees at Diamondbacks, 5:10 p.m., Cox, Ch. 34
Diamondbacks RHP Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77) vs. Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95).
At Chase Field: Pfaadt gave up six runs in 6⅔ innings against the Rangers in his most recent start. All six runs came in the fifth inning, in which Pfaadt was ruled to have missed the bag while covering first, opening the door for the final four runs of the inning to score. … Pfaadt has had a strong past few months overall, but his past five starts have been rough. He has posted a 5.74 ERA in 31⅓ innings in that stretch. … He has faced the Yankees only once in his career, giving up six runs (five earned) in 4⅓ innings in a game in 2023. … Schlittler looks like the favorite to win the American League Cy Young Award. He has the lowest ERA and WHIP and has logged 184⅔. … He has never faced the Diamondbacks. … Schlittler averages 98 mph with his four-seam fastball. He primarily throws that, his sinker and cutter, only occasionally sprinkling in curveballs and a rare slider.
Coming up
Sunday, Sept. 20: At Chase Field, 1:10 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Corbin Burnes (0-0, 5.87) vs. Yankees RHP Will Warren (10-6, 3.89).
Monday, Sept. 21: Off.
Tuesday, Sept. 22: At Colorado, 5:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Michael Soroka (8-5, 3.45) vs. Rockies LHP Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.38).
Wednesday, Sept. 23: At Colorado, 5:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00) vs. Rockies RHP Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09).

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees secured a 9-2 series-opening victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night.
Now, they're once again back in action on Saturday evening with right-handed ace and AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler on the mound for the Yankees, while the Diamondbacks will have righty Brandon Pfaadt pitching.
Ahead of the matchup, manager Aaron Boone didn't make any major changes to his starting lineup, but he did make some notable changes to his batting order.
Yankees Announce George Lombard Jr. Move
With outfielder Spencer Jones getting the day off and veteran Paul Goldschmidt out of the lineup after leading off on Friday, rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. is moving up in the batting order.
After hitting seventh in the series opener, Boone is placing Lombard Jr. in the five-hole Saturday, while Heliot Ramos bats cleanup and Ben Rice moves back into the leadoff role.
Cody Bellinger and Luis Garcia Jr. will remain in their normal roles, hitting second and third.
Here's the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: "Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP."
Yankees 9/19
B. Rice DH
C. Bellinger LF
L. García Jr. 1B
H. Ramos RF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
R. McMahon 3B
J. Caballero CF
C. Schlittler SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 19, 2026
Lombard Jr.'s 2026 Season
Since the Yankees called him up on Aug. 4, Lombard Jr. has exceeded expectations and made an immediate impact for New York.
He's appeared in 35 games and has gone 29-for-124 with 19 runs, four home runs, and 15 RBIs while hitting .234 with a .371 slugging percentage and a .663 OPS.
Looking at the Yankees
New York enters Saturday with an 89-64 overall record and currently holds the top Wild Card spot, which would set them up to host a Wild Card series at home in the Bronx.
That said, they're just 4.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East and the No. 1 overall seed in the AL, with an upcoming four-game set against the Rays this week.

item.content:encoded:
Last night was a good night for the Yankees, seeing the team put up five runs in the first paired with a good Gerrit Cole outing to cruise to a 9-2 win over the Diamondbacks. The club also picked up a game on the Rays as the AL East leaders dropped the opener of their series to the Red Sox. Tonight, the Yankees have two goals: get the win to stay in a hypothetically-competitive division race (all but necessary since Tampa Bay avenged the loss with a 2-1 win over Boston this afternoon), and build out a little more breathing room in the Cy Young race.
Dylan Cease had his worst start of the year on Friday for the Blue Jays, going just 2.2 innings and walking six. He and today's Yankee starter Cam Schlittler have had a heavyweight bout atop the Cy leaderboard all year, and while Cam's pulled away a bit in recent weeks, he can start to put the finishing touches on his case tonight. He hasn't allowed more than one earned run in a start since August 3rd (!!), making us all maybe expect a bit too much from the righty who can seemingly do no wrong. Schlittler has thrown 45 innings across those aforementioned seven starts, so he's not a five-and-fly guy, and his 1.00 ERA in that stretch is just…a farce.
Brandon Pfaadt is having the best season of his young career, with a 3.77 ERA and 4.06 FIP that are both significant steps forward after a pretty lost 2025. He doesn't strike many men out though, and a 45 percent ground ball rate means heavy sinking fastballs in the zone. There will be pitches to hit from Pfaadt; you just need to be able to elevate them.
Ben Rice had himself a fantastic game cleaning up last night and is bumped up to the leadoff spot tonight, with
Luis García Jr. getting the nod over Paul Goldschmidt at first base. Spencer Jones reportedly has a sore left foot, which means we get José Caballero in center, and I'm going to withhold comment on that decision for now.
It's an 8:10pm Eastern start but not a national broadcast, this one's on YES. The Diamondbacks will be celebrating their 2001 World Series championship throughout the evening, which seems kind of lame because you can't really "win" a championship when you didn't have an opponent.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees posted their starting lineup Saturday afternoon for the second game of a three-game set against the Arizona Diamondbacks, and Paul Goldschmidt was not in it.
New York is trying to take the series after a 9-2 win Friday night at Chase Field. Goldschmidt led off that game and finished with a hit, a walk and two runs scored.
The announced order put Ben Rice at designated hitter, Cody Bellinger in left field and Luis García Jr. at first base. Heliot Ramos started in right, George Lombard Jr. at shortstop, Austin Wells behind the plate, Anthony Volpe at second, Ryan McMahon at third and José Caballero in center. Cam Schlittler was listed as the starting pitcher.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP.”
Goldschmidt, a seven-time All-Star, is in his second season with the Yankees after signing a one-year deal in February. He entered Saturday hitting .253 with 85 hits, 18 home runs, 50 RBIs, 44 runs and one stolen base in 102 games.
The 39-year-old first baseman spent his first eight big-league seasons in Arizona. He made six straight All-Star teams from 2013 through 2018 while wearing a Diamondbacks uniform.
After leaving Phoenix, Goldschmidt spent six years with the St. Louis Cardinals and won National League Most Valuable Player honors in 2022.
The Yankees sit second in the American League East at 89-64 through 153 games. They have gone 8-2 in their last 10 and trail the Tampa Bay Rays by four games.
Arizona is third in the National League West at 80-74 after 154 games and 4-6 over its last 10.
Manager Aaron Boone has mixed Goldschmidt’s playing time throughout the second half as younger options such as Rice have taken on larger roles. Goldschmidt started Friday after sitting in recent games.
The veteran remains a respected presence in the clubhouse. The Yankees nominated him for the 2026 MLBPAA Heart and Hustle Award earlier this season.
Goldschmidt signed a one-year, $4 million contract with New York this past offseason after hitting .274 with 10 homers and 45 RBIs in 146 games during his first Yankees season.
He has 390 career home runs and 1,282 RBIs across 16 major-league seasons. Career numbers also include a .286 batting average and seven All-Star selections.
Saturday’s game was scheduled for late afternoon local time. A New York win would give the Yankees the series with one game left.
The Diamondbacks have struggled to find consistent production at first base this year after Goldschmidt left the organization years earlier.
New York continues to chase a postseason berth in the final weeks of the regular season. Goldschmidt’s availability as a pinch-hitter or late-inning option remains part of the roster mix even when he does not start.
The lineup change was posted hours before first pitch and immediately circulated among fans tracking the club’s late-season decisions.

item.content:encoded:
On Friday night, the New York Yankees beat the Arizona Diamondbacks (at Chase Field) by a score of 9-2.
Gerrit Cole got the start.
He allowed two earned runs in 6.0 innings (with six strikeouts).
Yankees Star Cole Makes Rice Statement
After the game, Cole was asked about Ben Rice (via YES Network).
Rice had two hits, including one home run and two walks.
Meredith Marakovits: “And Rice now, 39 home runs in the season. Just what have you thought of his production and what he has meant to this team?”
Cole: “Special, special year. Has made some really good adjustments from previous years going into this year. And I think he’s really started to kind of heat back up here the last few weeks after having to make some adjustments in the middle of the season. So not only is he really proficient with the bat, but he’s a smart player and a hard worker, which is leading him to have just a really outstanding season for us.”
Looking At Rice
Rice is in the middle of his third season at the MLB level (all with the Yankees).
He was picked in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft.
Right now, Rice is batting .264 with 144 hits, 39 home runs, 94 RBIs, 100 runs and three stolen bases in 146 games.
Looking At Cole
Cole is in the middle of his 6th season pitching for the Yankees.
He has also spent time with the Pittsburgh Pirates and Houston Astros.
Right now, Cole is 9-9 with a 3.63 ERA in 21 starts this year.
Looking At The Yankees Right Now
The Yankees (89-64) have two more games with the Diamondbacks before they return home to host the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday.
They are 4.0 games back of the Rays.

Access the Yankees beat like never before
Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
That was a slightly less definitive statement than what Judge consistently said during the summer when he was trying to come back from a right rib stress fracture, which he did after three-plus months on Sept. 8.
But now the clock is ticking even louder, with Saturday marking 10 days away from Game 1 of the American League wild card series.
“Definitely frustrated,” said Judge, who played seven games after missing 84 on the IL with the rib injury. “Dealt with strains before and kind of played through them, but this was in a different spot where it made it a little bit more difficult.”
Judge did not reveal what grade the strain was, but said it involved his Soleus muscle, which he indicated was more important to running and hitting compared to the gastrocnemius muscle.
“The focus is still the same, to be ready to go for October,” Judge said.
In the meantime, the Yankees are banking on their summer without Judge paying off now that he is back on the IL.
“Lean on each other,” Cody Bellinger said. “The game itself is hard; if you add too much pressure on yourself, the game becomes even harder. So we really just have to play for each other, lean on each other, pass the baton, do your job and control what you can control.”
The Yankees did that on Friday night, racing out of the gates to score five runs in the first inning of a 9-2 win against the Diamondbacks, just hours after the team announced Judge was going on the 10-day injured list with a right calf strain.
But they also got off well at the beginning of June after Judge landed on the IL with a right rib stress fracture before their lineup became a black hole for an extended stretch during the summer. They had finally started to break out of it shortly before Judge got back on Sept. 8, but after having him back for seven games, they now find themselves in the same spot again, less than two weeks away from the start of the playoffs.
“We’ve played most of the year this way, and I feel like in a lot of cases, especially some of our key guys over the last few weeks have started to, especially offensively, get it going like we know they’re capable of,” manager Aaron Boone said.
During the 84-game span that Judge missed this summer, the Yankees ranked 26th in runs per game (4.06), 29th in batting average (.227), 27th in OPS (.681), and 29th in WRC+ (90).
But over the tail end of that stretch, and into Judge’s return, the Yankees started to hit more like they are capable of. That included the trade deadline addition of Luis García Jr., the emergence of rookie outfielder Spencer Jones, and Bellinger getting back on track after returning from his own hamstring injury in August.
Perhaps most importantly, it has coincided with the reemergence of Ben Rice. The lefty slugger was a game wrecker for the first two months of the season before Judge went down, then cooled off a bit during the summer (albeit with some good stretches along the way) before catching fire again over the last few weeks. Entering Saturday, over his last 22 games, Rice had hit .353 with a 1.037 OPS and five home runs, including his 39th of the season Friday night.
“Special year,” Gerrit Cole said. “Has made some really good adjustments from previous years, going into this year, and I think he’s really started to heat back up here the last few weeks after having to make some adjustments in the middle of the season. Not only is he really proficient with the bat, but he’s a smart player and a hard worker, which is leading him to have a really outstanding season for us.”
The Yankees need that to continue for however long Judge is out (and even if and when he returns) for them to play deep into October, though Rice isn’t looking at it as having to do any more — which got some hitters in trouble during the three-time AL MVP’s first absence.
“I would think that everyone just goes out there and stays within themselves, tries to put together quality at-bat after quality at-bat,” he said. “Pitching is always going to be doing their thing, like they have for us all year. So from an offensive standpoint, just do what we did [Friday]: go out and have a team at-bat, trust the guy behind you and keep the line moving.”
To Rice’s point, the Yankees have leaned on the strength of their pitching staff all season, but that was especially the case during Judge’s three months on the IL this summer, when they were able to scratch out enough wins in low-scoring games, with their pitchers keeping them in it almost every night.
New York Post may be compensated and/or receive an affiliate commission if you buy something through our links.
“We have a lot of confidence in here,” Cole said. “For the most part of the summer, we’ve been tested really, really hard and we responded, by and large, really, really well. We have a lot of perfectionists in here. We’re always striving to be perfect and trying to be the best. But the reality is we’ve had a lot of obstacles we’ve had to overcome and, by and large, we’ve played really well.”

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Spencer Jones' remarkable stats vs. lefties are better than Yankees fans' wildest dreams
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: There were many questions the New York Yankees needed Spencer Jones to answer this season. Now, we've seen enough of him, even if it's been in a couple of disjointed stints, to get a good idea of who he is at the major league level. The answer: pretty damn good. item.content:encoded:
There were many questions the New York Yankees needed Spencer Jones to answer this season. Now, we've seen enough of him, even if it's been in a couple of disjointed stints, to get a good idea of who he is at the major league level.
The answer: pretty damn good. After struggling early, Jones has found his footing. A big reason for his ascendancy has been surprising. The Vanderbilt product has mashed left-handed pitching.
He's now logged 51 plate appearances against lefties and has slashed an eye-watering .435/.490/.761 following his homer off Minnesota Twins lefty specialist Taylor Rodgers on Sept. 15. It was the first dinger Rodgers gave up to a left-handed hitter over 133 plate appearances this season.
The sample size isn't huge, but it's relatively significant. For example, Ben Rice has 209 plate appearances against lefties out of his 622 plate appearances. For Jones, the 51 matchups against southpaws are a decent portion of his 255 total plate appearances.
One of the most impressive things about how he's performed against same-handed pitching is the amount of power he's demonstrated. Obviously, the six-foot-seven outfielder is a behemoth, but most lefties, even those who perform well against southpaws, see a drop in power in those situations. Take Rice, for instance; his slugging percentage drops from .561 against righties to .457 against left-handers. That hasn't been the case for Jones.
This has just been one part of Jones' maturation process that should have every fan feeling confident about not only his future, but his ability to contribute now.
Spencer Jones' performance against lefties has Yankees well-positioned for playoffs vs. Red Sox
Overall, Jones is hitting .259/.331/.452 with 10 homers on the season. He's been even better since being recalled on July 22, posting a .271/.337/.490 line with eight of his 10 homers coming during this most recent span.
There should be no more doubt that he should start over Trent Grisham, assuming Grisham is healthy, once the playoffs roll around. A significant part of that reasoning has to do with his performance against southpaws.
Jones has learned a lot from Cody Bellinger on how to handle those tough at-bats since he's been up in the bigs and the star left fielder has been healthy.
“When we are in the dugout, he’s one of those people I can go up to and ask, like, ‘Yo, what did you see?’ He’ll tell me bluntly what he saw, how he saw it, and essentially what he’s going to do next time. It’s like, all right, good to know before I go even into my first (at-bat) what this MVP is going to do for his first at-bat. It’s pretty sweet knowing that I’ve got these guys to help me out,” Jones said to The Athletic this week.
He couldn't have a better mentor. Bellinger isn't hitting lefties as much as he did last year, when he put up an insane .353/.415/.601 line, but his .287/.346/.449 performance in 2026 is plenty good, and better than what he's done against righties. In fact, Bellinger is about as balanced as they come with an .804 career OPS against left-handers and an .819 mark against righties.
We spoke about Rice earlier, but the early-season drama about his usage against lefties is a thing of the past. While he has more pop against righties, Rice's .255/.330/.457 line against southpaws is more than serviceable.
Despite having so many lefties in the lineup on a daily basis, the Yankees as a whole don't suffer much from it. The club is hitting a collective .247/.318/.422 against left-handed pitching this season, with a .740 OPS that ranks ninth. Remember, for most of that time, Aaron Judge hasn't been a factor, either.
Looking ahead, the Yankees' most likely opponent in the Wild Card series is the Red Sox, who are loaded with left-handers. In the rotation, they boast southpaws Payton Tolle and Ranger Suárez, with their being a possibility that Jake Bennett makes the cut, too. In the bullpen, they'll hope to unleash Garrett Crochet, Erik Miller and old friend Aroldis Chapman.
However, rather than being overmatched, we might say that this plays into the Yankees' hands. New York can handle left-handed pitching, and those lefty bats can tee off against righties. Jones emerging as a threat against southpaws only solidifies the strength and gives the Yankees another regular who doesn't need a platoon partner, allowing them to match up only where they're vulnerable.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are in the middle of a three-game series against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix.
New York won the first game of the series 9-2 on Friday. Game 2 is slated to begin at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday.
Before Saturday’s game, the Yankees announced a surprising lineup decision involving José Caballero.
New York Yankees Announce Interesting José Caballero Decision
Surprisingly, José Caballero will start in center field for the Yankees on Saturday. Caballero has played 11 innings in center this season and recorded 15 innings at the position last year.
Meanwhile, Spencer Jones, the Yankees’ primary center fielder, is out of the lineup with a sore left foot.
The New York Post’s Greg Joyce wrote on X: Spencer Jones said he’s dealing with a sore left foot, which he chalked up to the wear-and-tear from playing on turf. But downplayed it, said he’s fine, just getting a day. “It’s no big deal,” Jones said.
Here is the Yankees’ full lineup for Saturday:
- Ben Rice DH
- Cody Bellinger LF
- Luis Garcia Jr. 1B
- Heliot Ramos RF
- George Lombard Jr. SS
- Austin Wells C
- Anthony Volpe 2B
- Ryan McMahon 3B
- José Caballero CF
Starting Pitcher: RHP Cam Schlittler
Here is the Diamondbacks’ lineup:
- Laars Nootbar LF
- Ketel Marte 2B
- Gabriel Moreon C
- Geraldo Perdomo SS
- Corbin Carroll RF
- Nolan Arenado 3B
- Tim Tawa 1B
- Jesus Sanchez DH
- Jordan Lawlar CF
Starting Pitcher: Brandon Pfaadt
New York Yankees Right Now
In the division standings, New York is four games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East.
Next, the Yankees are slated to play the Diamondbacks at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday. The series will wrap up on Sunday afternoon.
The Yankees will finish the season by hosting the Tampa Bay Rays for four games, and then the Baltimore Orioles for three games.
If the standings hold up, the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card round.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Three questions for Aaron Judge and the Yankees as injury casts doubt on slugger's playoff availability
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa
item.description: Friday was a bad day for the New York Yankees even though they opened their final road series of the regular season with a blowout win (NYY 9, ARI 2). item.content:encoded:
Friday was a bad day for the New York Yankees even though they opened their final road series of the regular season with a blowout win (NYY 9, ARI 2). Captain Aaron Judge is less than two weeks after returning from a fractured rib that sidelined him more than three months. Judge's status for the rest of the season is up in the air.
"I don't have a timeline on him. I'm not going to predict anything. We'll just obviously treat it and see what transpires," manager Aaron Boone said (via MLB.com). "... The reality is, we've had to play a lot of the season this year without him. There's no replacing a player who is as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations. Those don't change now."
The Yankees are always cagey about Judge's injuries. They declined to reveal the severity of the calf strain or give a timetable for his return. Generally speaking, Grade 1 calf strains (the least severe) require 2-3 weeks on the injured list, though calves are very tricky and easy to reinjury. They must be allowed to heal fully, otherwise you risk a more severe injury.
For all intents and purposes, the Yankees are locked into the top wild-card spot. They're six games up in the loss column on the Boston Red Sox, who currently sit in the second wild card spot, plus the Yankees won the season series and have the tiebreaker, so it's really a seven-game lead. New York can clinch the top wild-card spot as soon as Sunday.
The AL East title remains mathematically possible, but it is a long shot. The Yankees are four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the loss column with four head-to-head games remaining next week in the Bronx. The Rays only need to win one of those four games to clinch the season series and secure the tiebreaker, upping the difficulty for New York.
Just to lay it all out, here's what needs to happen for the Yankees to win the AL East, assuming they sweep those four games against the Rays and clinch the tiebreaker for themselves, which is a pretty big assumption:
- Rays go 6-3 or better: Rays win AL East
- Rays go 5-4: Yankees must go 9-0
- Rays go 4-5: Yankees must go 8-1
- Rays go 3-6: Yankees must go 7-2
- Rays go 2-7: Yankees must go 6-3
- Rays go 1-8: Yankees must go 5-4
- Rays go 0-9: Yankees must go 4-5
The Yankees have already clinched a postseason spot and winning the AL East was a long shot even with Judge. These last nine regular-season games are almost meaningless. If the AL East race gets interesting in a few days, the Yankees can shift gears, but the big picture takes priority this next week. Resting key relievers, lining up the rotation for the Wild Card Series, etc.
"Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he's the best hitter in the game," Cody Bellinger said (via MLB.com). "For us in here, our mindset is, we're going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I'm fully confident that we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win, and beat anybody."
With the postseason less than two weeks away, Judge's calf injury creates a lot of questions for both him and the Yankees overall. Here are three questions for the man himself, and his team.
Three questions for Judge
1. Will he return for the postseason? This is really the only question, right? The Yankees are built around Judge being the best hitter in the world, and when he's not, the walls begin to cave in. New York had one of the lowest-scoring offenses in baseball when Judge was out with his rib injury. To paraphrase another New York baseball legend, Judge is the straw that stirs the drink.
Judge is eligible to come off the injured list next Sunday, the final day of the regular season. Roster-wise, he can return in time for the postseason. Health-wise, we have no idea. Calf strains are rarely 10-day absences, but that's what the Yankees have to hope is the case here. There's a very real chance the Yankees are without Judge for at least the Wild Card Series, and maybe longer.
“I’d like to be back by the postseason,” Aaron Judge said. “That’s definitely the plan.”
Said the calf strain involves the soleus muscle — which he said is more crucial to running and hitting — making it more difficult to play through.
2. Will he be himself at the plate? Judge did not go on a minor-league rehab assignment before returning from the rib injury and it showed. He went 4 for 23 (.174) with one walk and 13 strikeouts in his seven games back before the calf injury. His timing was not there at all. Judge's one homer came on a hanging breaking ball. Otherwise, pitchers threw fastballs by him consistently.
To put a number on it, Judge missed with 41% of his swings against fastballs in his seven games back, more than double the 19% league average. This is what it looks like when you miss with more than two out of every five swings against heaters:
It is not exactly a surprise a hitter who did not go on a rehab assignment after spending more than three months on the shelf looked out of sorts at the plate. Judge and the Yankees knew it would take him some time to get back up to speed at the plate, and they were willing to live with it. The goal was always to be ready for the postseason, not so much the regular season.
These last nine games aren't particularly important for the Yankees in the standings, but they were incredibly important to Judge. He needed at-bats to rediscover his timing at the plate, and get back to being the dominant hitter he's been throughout his career. The calf strain puts that on pause. Judge now has even fewer at-bats available to get back to being himself.
3. Will he be able to play the field? There is a scenario in which Judge plays through the calf strain as a full-time DH who doesn't run at 100% (or close to it). How the Yankees would align their defense in that scenario, I have no idea. Ben Rice is a full-time DH these days and also New York's best non-Judge hitter. Platoon-mates Luis Gárcia Jr. and Paul Goldschmidt are first basemen.
Unless the Yankees do something unexpected, like put Gárcia back at second base (where he was terrible defensively) or Rice back behind the plate (where he was also terrible defensively), slotting Judge in at DH means one of the team's most productive hitters will have to sit. This is something the Yankees will worry about when the time comes, and not a second sooner.
Three questions for the Yankees
1. Where will the righty pop come from? The Yankees have a very lefty-heavy lineup and Judge's righty heft provides important balance. Only the Cleveland Guardians have gotten fewer plate appearances from righties this season. Friday's lineup against Arizona Diamondbacks lefty Eduardo Rodriguez could be what the Yankees run out there against lefties in October:
- 1B Paul Goldschmidt, RHB
- LF Cody Bellinger, LHB
- RF Heliot Ramos, RHB
- DH Ben Rice, LHB
- 3B Amed Rosario, RHB
- CF Spencer Jones, LHB
- SS George Lombard Jr., RHB
- C Austin Wells, LHB
- 2B Anthony Volpe, RHB
Goldschmidt and Ramos are lefty mashers. Bellinger and Rice are very productive left-on-left hitters. Jones has performed well against lefties as a big leaguer, though his minor-league track record against southpaws isn't great. Rosario is having his worst season against lefties. The 7-8-9 spots are unlikely to make an impact offensively, regardless of the pitcher's handedness.
That lineup would look much more imposing with Judge in the No. 3 spot. Perhaps this is not such a big concern though? Since trade deadline day, the Yankees have the highest batting average (.289) and on-base percentage (.362) against lefties, and the third-highest slugging percentage (.456) despite Judge not playing much, and not being much of a factor when he did play.
In all likelihood the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series, and Boston has three quality lefty starters (Jake Bennett, Ranger Suárez, Payton Tolle) and a shutdown lefty relief tandem (Aroldis Chapman, Erik Miller). To beat the Red Sox, the Yankees will need their righty hitters to produce, and now the status of their best right-handed hitter is in question.
2. Will the pitching hold up? Despite not having Judge for more than three months, the Yankees have the American League's best run differential (+143) and second-best record (89-64). They can thank their pitching staff. New York has allowed only 3.68 runs per game this year, the fewest in baseball. Since trade deadline day, it's an incredible 3.37 runs allowed per game.
There are some cracks beginning to form, however. Gerrit Cole has surrendered eight home runs in his last three starts, including five on a four-seam fastball that is no longer the dominant pitch it was at his peak. Max Fried's velocity has been down a tick since returning from a bone bruise in his elbow late last month. That injury has sent him to the injured list twice this year.
Cam Schlittler, the AL Cy Young favorite, has thrown a career-high 184 ⅔ innings with two regular-season starts remaining, plus the postseason. Key late-inning relievers Paul Blackburn, David Bednar, and Brent Headrick have worked a lot -- A LOT -- this season and have all shown a slight dip in velocity in recent weeks, which perhaps is a sign the workload is catching up to them.
Without Judge (and sometimes even with him), the Yankees are a run prevention team. Their superpower is a suffocating pitching staff that is among the best in baseball at limiting hard contact, particularly in the air. With Judge absent, the pitching staff and the ability to prevent runs in general will be of paramount importance. No Judge reduces the margin of error considerably.
3. What about their other injured players? Judge is not the only injured Yankee. Center field Trent Grisham has not played since Sept. 4 due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain. On Friday, Boone said Grisham is pretty far into his running program, and he could make it back before the end of the regular season. That would give the outfield a lift should Judge miss extended time.
Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. has not played since jamming his thumb sliding into second base on Sept. 8. Boone said Chisholm will come off the injured list when the Yankees return home next week. He's had a down year overall, but Chisholm was playing his best baseball of the season right before the injury. He's an important presence given his speed and defense in particular.
Left-hander Ryan Weathers is working his way back from a flexor strain. He last pitched Aug. 22. Weathers is throwing bullpen sessions, though Boone confirmed he won't return during the regular season. If/when Weathers does return, it will be as a reliever. He has bullpen experience and the Yankees could use middle relief help, but Weathers has to make it back first.
At minimum, Chisholm and Grisham would give the Yankees more options for their Judge-less lineup, even if they only platoon. It wouldn't be hard to find a role for Weathers, who had allowed no more than one run in six of his last seven starts before the injury. Bottom line though, the Yankees need Judge. Everything else is secondary to his return and effectiveness.

item.title: [bolavip.com] NY Yankees’ Aaron Boone expresses full confidence in Cam Schlittler’s Cy Young candidacy
item.dc:creator: Santiago Tovar
item.description: For a historic franchise like the New York Yankees, rotation stability is paramount over the long haul of a 162-game season. That makes Cam Schlittler’s dominant breakout campaign all the more remarkable—so much so that manager Aaron Boone believes the young right-hander has built a compelling case to take home the American League Cy Young Award. When asked about Schlittler’s transformative presence in the rotation, Boone didn’t mince words: “Well, he’s gonna win the Cy Young!” The manager’s rin
item.content:encoded:
For a historic franchise like the New York Yankees, rotation stability is paramount over the long haul of a 162-game season. That makes Cam Schlittler’s dominant breakout campaign all the more remarkable—so much so that manager Aaron Boone believes the young right-hander has built a compelling case to take home the American League Cy Young Award.
When asked about Schlittler’s transformative presence in the rotation, Boone didn’t mince words: “Well, he’s gonna win the Cy Young!” The manager’s ringing endorsement underscores just how dominant Schlittler has been on the mound this year.
While Boone continues to navigate rotation depth with Ryan Weathers sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Schlittler gives the Yankees a legitimate ace to rely on as they gear up for October.
On the offensive side, Boone is also monitoring the return timeline for slugger Aaron Judge, who was sidelined with a calf strain. In the meantime, the Yankees skipper has relied on depth options like Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger to keep the lineup producing.
Key milestones driving Schlittler’s Cy Young case
A stellar 2026 breakout campaign with the Yankees has vaulted Schlittler directly into the front-runner conversation for the American League Cy Young Award. Stepping up as the de facto ace while Gerrit Cole missed time, Schlittler has delivered elite run suppression, swing-and-miss stuff, and exceptional durability.
Here is a breakdown of the key numbers and milestones anchoring Schlittler’s Cy Young candidacy:
- 1.95 ERA: Schlittler took over the MLB ERA lead in September, standing as the only qualified starter with an ERA under 2.00.
- Historical run: His 1.71 ERA through his first 16 starts marked the lowest ERA by a Yankees starter through that stretch since Hall of Famer Whitey Ford in 1964.
- 228 Strikeouts in 184.2 IP (11.1 K/9): Schlittler eclipsed the 200-strikeout mark on August 28 against Boston, becoming the fourth-youngest pitcher in franchise history to achieve the feat.
- Signature outings: Highlighted by a career-high 13-strikeout performance against the Cincinnati Reds on June 19, along with double-digit strikeout shutouts against Philadelphia (12 K) and Atlanta (11 K).
Other top Cy Young contenders
Schlittler isn’t running unopposed in a tightly contested American League race. Strong campaigns from power arm Dylan Cease of the Toronto Blue Jays and left-hander Garrett Crochet of the Boston Red Sox keep them firmly in the mix.
Over in the National League, the Cy Young field features plenty of heavy hitters, headlined by Milwaukee Brewers phenom Jacob Misiorowski, Atlanta Braves veteran Chris Sale, and the Philadelphia Phillies duo of Cristopher Sanchez and Jesus Luzardo.

item.content:encoded:
Designated hitter Ben Rice hit his 39th home run of the season as the New York Yankees beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 at Chase Field in Phoenix on Friday night.
Following the win, Yankees manager Aaron Boone claimed he predicted Rice would hit 39 home runs this year.
New York Yankees Manager Aaron Boone Made Bold Ben Rice Prediction That Came True
"Thirty-nine [home runs] was my prediction. I swear. So I'm hoping he goes sailing on by that," Boone said. He's been great. You look up at his numbers, and it's an elite season. Really here of late, over the last three or four weeks, after a little bit of a lull there, he's found his stride again. I feel like he's having great at-bats every night."
"39 was my prediction!"
Aaron Boone tells @M_Marakovits he anticipated a big year from Ben Rice at the beginning of the season. pic.twitter.com/iMNLIOK3FE
— YES Network (@YESNetwork) September 19, 2026
Rice, 27, is having the best season of his young career. He made his first career All-Star Game this season and has posted 3.6 bWAR and an .897 OPS with 39 home runs and 94 RBI over 146 games.
Rice was asked if he knew about Boone's preseason prediction after the win.
"Yeah, he said something in spring training I feel like. 'We really want you to get out there and hit 39 [home runs] for us.' So I know what he was doing," Rice said. "He was trying to get under my skin a little bit. He likes to short you one short you two of maybe what your goal would be."
New York Yankees Right Now
The Yankees' record improved to 89-64 after Friday's win over the Diamondbacks.
New York has a 5 1/2-game lead over the Boston Red Sox for the top Wild Card spot.
In the division standings, New York is four games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East.
Next, the Yankees are slated to play the Diamondbacks at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday. The series will wrap up on Sunday afternoon.
The Yankees will finish the season by hosting the Tampa Bay Rays for four games, and then the Baltimore Orioles for three games.
If the standings hold up, the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card round.

Ben Rice dispara su jonrón 39 y los Yankees superan a los D-Backs
El artillero remolca 2 vueltas, llega a 94 y Nueva York se impone 9 por 2 a Arizona, equipo que se aleja de la batalla por clasificar
Ben Rice conectó su 39no jonrón de la temporada, Gerrit Cole se convirtió en la primera selección global del draft con más victorias y los Yankees de Nueva York aprovecharon una primera entrada de cinco carreras para tomar el control temprano y vencer 9-2 a los Diamondbacks de Arizona la noche del viernes.

Los primeros cinco bateadores de Nueva York se embasaron ante el zurdo All-Star de los D-backs, el venezolano Eduardo Rodríguez, y un sencillo de dos carreras de George Lombard Jr. puso la pizarra 5-0. Lombard añadió un jonrón solitario en la sexta y terminó con tres carreras impulsadas.
Cole (9-9) se recuperó tras un par de aperturas en las que permitió siete cuadrangulares —la mayor cantidad que ha concedido en un lapso de dos juegos. Permitió dos carreras y cuatro imparables en seis entradas, y ponchó a seis.
Elegido primero por Pittsburgh en 2011, Cole consiguió su victoria número 162. Es una más que Mike Moore, seleccionado como número 1 por Seattle en 1981.
Rodríguez (15-7) eligió un mal momento para tener, posiblemente, su peor apertura de la temporada: necesitó 45 lanzamientos para conseguir tres outs, su cifra más alta en una primera entrada. Permitió siete carreras, cinco hits y otorgó cuatro bases por bolas en 5 1/3 entradas. _

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees’ Gerrit Cole Sets All-Time MLB Record
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen

item.content:encoded:
For a little while, it looked like it might be yet another rough outing for Gerrit Cole as the New York Yankees get closer to the playoffs.
Cole allowed a two-run home run to Arizona Diamondbacks superstar Corbin Carroll in the bottom of the second inning.
The Yankees had spotted Cole a five-run lead, but with the way the veteran right-hander has pitched lately, that didn't feel as safe as it potentially would've in the past.
On this Friday night, though, Cole was sharp from there. He didn't allow another run.
Cole eventually went 6.0 innings to earn a quality start, allowing four hits and those two runs while not walking any hitters. He struck out six while improving his season record to 9-9 and his ERA to 3.63.
Ryan Yarbrough, Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil polished the game off out of New York's bullpen in a 9-2 win that improved the Yankees to 89-64.
This night was about a lot of Yankees, including Ben Rice with a triple and a home run, and George Lombard Jr. with a home run as part of a five-run first.
But the most crucial thing that happened for New York was that Cole found his groove again. They'll need him sharp in the playoffs, and with only a couple more outings for him before then, this was a great step in the right direction.
Cole also made a fun bit of history in the process.
Gerrit Cole's New MLB History
Cole has now won the most games in an MLB career for any pitcher drafted No. 1 overall, according to MLB's Sarah Langs.
This was the 162nd pitching win of Cole's career.
The previous record was held by Mike Moore, who won 161 games after being the first overall pick in 1981.
David Price holds third place on the list with 157 wins after going in the top spot in 2007.
Cole can now expand on this record going forward, and considering how many fewer pitching wins starting pitchers are getting in this era, he probably has a chance to push the record out of reach if he has a few more solid seasons.
Gerrit Cole Draft
Cole was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2011 MLB Draft out of UCLA.
Four pitchers began the 2011 draft. The Mariners picked lefty Danny Hultzen out of Virginia second. The Diamondbacks chose Cole's UCLA teammate Trevor Bauer third. And the Orioles snagged high school righty Dylan Bundy fourth.
The first hitter chosen was high school outfielder Bubba Starling to the Royals at the fifth pick.
The National stook Rice slugger Anthony Rendon at No. 6.
The Diamondbacks were back on the board at No. 7 to get Archie Bradley, a high school righty.
The back-to-back picks at Nos. 8 and 9 were Francisco Lindor and Javier Baez to the Indians and Cubs, then the Padres got Cory Spangenberg at No. 11 before the Astros chose George Springer with the 11th pick.
It was a fascinating start to a draft, to be sure, with Cole living up to his hype.

The post Yankees' Gerrit Cole Sets All-Time MLB Record appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
Gerrit Cole disipó las dudas sobre su rendimiento actual tras firmar una sólida actuación desde el montículo en la victoria 9-2 de los Yankees de Nueva York frente a los Cascabeles de Arizona. El derecho, quien venía de una racha complicada con los cuadrangulares, ajustó y mostró su mejor cara en la jornada del viernes.
La ofensiva neoyorquina respaldó de inmediato a su abridor con un racimo de cinco anotaciones en el propio primer episodio ante el criollo Eduardo Rodríguez. Sencillos remolcadores de Amed Rosario y George Lombard Jr., sumados a un boleto con bases llenas de Ben Rice, le dieron la ventaja a los «Bombarderos del Bronx» desde el comienzo.
Lombard Jr. completó una jornada destacada al impulsar tres carreras, incluyendo un bambinazo en el sexto tramo. Por su parte, Rice también lució con el madero al conectar su jonrón número 39 de la temporada regular, consolidándose como el líder del equipo en ese apartado.
El único daño que permitió Cole llegó en el segundo inning mediante un cuadrangular de dos carreras de Corbin Carroll. Sin embargo, el serpentinero ajustó el brazo y maniató por completo a la toletería de los D-backs durante el resto de su labor.
Leer también: Mookie Betts comanda con dos jonrones noche de cinco vuelacercas
Con este resultado, los Yankees (89-64) sumaron su triunfo número 11 en sus últimos 15 compromisos y se colocaron a cuatro juegos de los Rays de Tampa Bay en la pelea por el Este de la Liga Americana, mostrando solvencia ofensiva para suplir la ausencia por lesión de Aaron Judge.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Yankees' 39-homer reality is making October very awkward
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson

item.content:encoded:
Ben Rice went 2-for-3 with a homer, a triple and two walks in the Yankees’ 9-2 win over Arizona on Thursday. He also gave the club something more complicated than a nice September box score.
Rice is sitting on 39 homers, 94 RBI and an .897 OPS in 146 games. A 39-homer season is not a profile the Yankees can squeeze into a convenient role once the postseason lineup gets trimmed.
I would stop treating him like the left-handed option who can be used when the matchup happens to work. The volume is too large now.
Yankees have a 39-homer problem
Ben Rice has earned the big at-bats. He has also made first base and designated hitter a far more crowded place than anyone expected back in April.
There are no style points for leaving a bat with that kind of production on the bench because a veteran has been there before. October decisions are about who gives the lineup its best chance on that night. Rice has created a serious claim on those spots.
The Yankees need to lean into the production
The fair concern is obvious. September numbers do not guarantee an October heater, and Rice still has to carry this against better pitching when every matchup gets picked apart.
But the other side deserves equal weight. He is not trying to rescue a disappointing year with one good week. This has been a full season of damage, and Thursday added another loud entry to it.
The Yankees can figure out the defensive alignment later. The bigger mistake would be acting like 39 homers are disposable.
Rice has forced the issue. Now the Yankees have to make a real choice.
More about:New York Yankees

item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Gerrit Cole makes history in win vs. Diamondbacks appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
New York Yankees starter Gerrit Cole made MLB history in Friday night's 9-2 win against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
The 36-year-old earned his 162nd career victory, moving past Mike Moore's 161 wins for the most ever by a pitcher who was selected No. 1 overall in the MLB Draft. Cole was chosen first by the Pittsburgh Pirates in 2011, while Moore went to the Seattle Mariners with the top selection in 1981. David Price is next on the list, ranking third with 157 career wins.
The milestone came as Cole bounced back after allowing seven home runs across his previous two starts, the highest two-game figure of his career. He also had surrendered leadoff home runs in each of those outings.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
After working on his delivery and potential pitch-tipping issues since his previous start against the New York Mets, Cole retired Arizona in order during a 12-pitch opening inning. Corbin Carroll later hit a two-run homer on a four-seam fastball that missed its location, but Cole gave up nothing else to the Diamondbacks.
The right-hander completed six innings, allowing two runs and four hits while issuing no walks and striking out six. He threw 90 pitches, with 62 going for strikes, finishing with a 9-9 record.
New York provided Cole with plenty of early support, sending its first five hitters to base against Eduardo Rodriguez during a five-run opening inning. Ben Rice drew a bases-loaded walk, Amed Rosario delivered an RBI single and George Lombard Jr. added a two-run single.
Rice later launched his 39th homer of the season in the third inning, while Lombard hit his own solo shot in the sixth and finished with three RBIs.
The Yankees improved to 89-64 and moved within four games of the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East with nine games remaining. New York had already secured a postseason berth and has now won 11 of its last 15 games.
Manager Aaron Boone also confirmed that Cole should receive a start if the Yankees reach the American League Wild Card Series.
Related: Yankees manager Aaron Boone drops huge Cam Schlittler Cy Young prediction

item.title: [ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos] Ben Rice hits 39th homer, Cole becomes winningest No. 1 draft pick as Yanks cruise past D-backs 9-2
item.source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
item.dc:creator: ABC News; DAVID BRANDT AP baseball writer
item.description: Ben Rice hits 39th homer, Cole becomes winningest No. 1 draft pick as Yanks cruise past D-backs 9-2 Ben Rice hit his 39th homer of the season, Gerrit Cole became the winningest No. 1 overall draft pick and the New York Yankees used a five-run first inning to take control early and beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 PHOENIX -- Ben Rice hit his 39th homer of the season, Gerrit Cole became the winningest No. 1 overall draft pick and the New York Yankees used a five-run first inning to take control e
item.content:encoded:
Ben Rice hits 39th homer, Cole becomes winningest No. 1 draft pick as Yanks cruise past D-backs 9-2
Ben Rice hit his 39th homer of the season, Gerrit Cole became the winningest No. 1 overall draft pick and the New York Yankees used a five-run first inning to take control early and beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2
PHOENIX -- Ben Rice hit his 39th homer of the season, Gerrit Cole became the winningest No. 1 overall draft pick and the New York Yankees used a five-run first inning to take control early and beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 on Friday night.
After learning three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge was headed back to the injured list with a right calf strain, the Yankees won for the eighth time in 10 games. New York, which has already clinched a playoff spot, is four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East with nine games remaining.
The D-backs' have lost three straight and their playoff hopes are in major trouble. They're five games back of the final NL wild card with eight games left.
New York's first five batters reached against D-backs' All-Star left hander Eduardo Rodriguez and George Lombard Jr.'s two-run single made it 5-0. Lombard added a solo homer in the sixth and finished with three RBIs.
Cole (9-9) bounced back from a pair of starts that saw him surrender seven homers — the most he's ever given up over a two-game span. He gave up two runs and four hits in six innings, striking out six.
Selected first by Pittsburgh in 2011, Cole won his 162nd game. That is one more than Mike Moore, picked No. 1 by Seattle in 1981.
Rodriguez (15-7) picked a bad time to have arguably his worst start this season, needing 45 pitches to get three outs, his career high for a first inning. He gave up seven runs, five hits and four walks over 5 1/3 innings.
Corbin Carroll hit a two-run homer to cut the deficit to 5-2 in the second. Rice's solo homer in the third pushed the Yankees ahead 6-2.
The D-backs send RHP Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77 ERA) to the mound Saturday night while the Yankees counter with RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95).
