item.title: [Yahoo Sports] No Aaron Judge, no problem? Yankees show they're still a force to be reckoned with
item.dc:creator: Bob Nightengale; USA TODAY
item.description: PHOENIX — Just in case anyone thought the New York Yankees would simply fade away into the night, their season drifting out to sea with the news that Aaron Judge may be done for the season, the Bronx Bombers delivered a subtle message Friday night that reverberated around the baseball world. The Yankees, with Gerrit Cole looking more like the 2023 Cy Young winner than the pitcher who looked like he was throwing batting practice earlier this month, smacked around the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 Frid
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Just in case anyone thought the New York Yankees would simply fade away into the night, their season drifting out to sea with the news that Aaron Judge may be done for the season, the Bronx Bombers delivered a subtle message Friday night that reverberated around the baseball world.
The Yankees, with Gerrit Cole looking more like the 2023 Cy Young winner than the pitcher who looked like he was throwing batting practice earlier this month, smacked around the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 Friday, and acted afterwards as if it was simply business as usual.
There was Cole, who had given up seven homers in his last two starts pitching his best game in a month, yielding four hits and two runs in six innings.
There was DH Ben Rice, looking like a top-5 MVP candidate by hitting his 39th home run of the season − just as Yankees manager Aaron Boone predicted in spring training − to go along with 94 RBI.
There was rookie shortstop George Lombard, hitting a homer and playing flawless defense.
And there were the Yankees, talking as if they plan to be playing deep into October, whether Judge is in uniform or on their bench as a cheerleader. Judge is going on the injured list with a strained calf and the Yankees have no idea whether he'll return.
"I mean, it's a tough blow for us to take,'' Rice said. "Obviously, we were missing him for a long time there (three months), so this one is especially hard to swallow, just being back for a brief period and already gone.
"But we got no choice but to just keep playing hard, keeping doing our thing.''
Well, that starts on the mound, and with Cole dominating Friday, with Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler scheduled Saturday, and Max Fried and Carlos Rodon pitching well, there may not be a more formidable starting rotation in the postseason.
Cole, 9-9 with a 3.63 ERA in his first season back from Tommy John surgery, certainly knows there's room for improvement. But after being belted around with a 7.15 ERA his past two starts, giving up seven homers and 15 hits in 11.1 innings, this was a massive improvement.
"I thought he was really good,'' Boone said. "You know he grinded pretty hard. Between the last start and this one, there are subtle adjustments you make that a lot of people probably over-reacted to.
"The reality is he's having an outstanding season. He's throwing the ball really well, and a great pitcher like him is going to be able to make some adjustments.''
Cole, who missed the entire 2025 season and the first 51 games this year, says he modified his mechanics to remake his delivery. Why, except for missing his location on a low fastball to Corbin Carroll in the second inning, resulting in a two-run homer, he was on-point with virtually all of his other pitches. He threw 90 pitches − 62 for strikes − without walking a batter.
"I mean, I don't think we did a perfect job tonight,'' Cole said. "I think we moved the needle in the right direction. I think there's some meat on the bone there. It's not easy, but it's necessary. It's the big leagues.''
Yep, just like no one is going to feel sorry for the Yankees with the loss of Judge. Not the Tampa Bay Rays, who are still in first place with a four-game lead. Not the Boston Red Sox, who the Yankees likely will face in the first round. Not a soul outside the Yankees organization.
"We have a lot of confidence in here,'' Cole said. "I mean, for the most part of the summer, we've been tested really, really hard, and responded − by and large − really well.
"We have a lot of perfectionists in here. We're always trying to be perfect, and always striving to be the best. But the reality is we've had a lot of obstacles that we've had to overcome, and we've played really well. So we're looking forward to more challenges to come.''
Yes, with or without Judge. The Yankees went 46-39 when he was out 100 days with a rib fracture, and they believe they're built for October. They know they have four top-quality starters and a deep bullpen that can dominate anyone.
"That's probably our biggest strength,'' Boone said. "Whoever we hand the ball to every day, we know is going to give us an opportunity to win a game.''
They proved that this night, with Judge merely watching from the bench, knowing he may have played his final game of the season.
"We're obviously bummed for Aaron, and Aaron's probably bummed too,'' Cole said, "but we've been in this position before this year. Unfortunately, it's our reality at this point.''
Follow Nightengale on X: @Bnightengale
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: No Aaron Judge, no problem? Yankees show they're still a force to be reckoned with

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Dos noches antes, la pelota se le había escapado por debajo del guante y había contribuido a que los Yankees cayeran derrotados en un partido de 13 entradas. El novato se lo tomó muy a pecho. El viernes, George Lombard Jr. respondió de la única forma en que puede hacerlo un jugador joven: con un bate lo suficientemente contundente como para ahogar ese recuerdo.
Conectó un sencillo de dos carreras en la primera entrada. Se llevó un jonrón en la sexta. Al final de la noche, sumaba dos hits y tres carreras impulsadas, y el campocorto que parecía desconcertado en Minnesota se mostraba ahora como una pieza clave del equipo.
La coincidencia fue casi cruel por su simetría. La misma tarde en que el equipo se preparaba para recibir el golpe más duro por una lesión en meses, su jugador titular menos consolidado cuajó su partido más sólido.
Lo que podría haber sido un golpe bajo se convirtió en toda una declaración de intenciones. Y esa declaración no tuvo casi nada que ver con el hombre por el que todos estaban preocupados.
Los Yankees arrollaron a los Diamondbacks por 9-2 en el Chase Field el viernes por la noche, unas horas después de enterarse de que Aaron Judge volvería a la lista de lesionados por una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha que podría poner fin a su temporada regular. Nueva York mejoró su balance a 89-64, sumó su undécima victoria en 15 partidos y se colocó a cuatro partidos de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, después de que los Rays perdieran 4-2 ante Boston. Los Yankees también mantuvieron una ventaja de 5 partidos y medio sobre los Red Sox por el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana.
Una primera entrada de cinco carreras en la que no hizo falta ninguna superestrella
El modelo a seguir para una vida sin Judge quedó claro enseguida. Los Yankees enviaron a 10 bateadores al plato contra el zurdo de Arizona, Eduardo Rodríguez, y anotaron cinco veces antes de que se produjera el segundo out.
Los cinco primeros bateadores llegaron a base. Paul Goldschmidt consiguió una base por bolas , Cody Bellinger conectó un sencillo y, tras otra base por bolas, Ben Rice consiguió una base por bolas con las bases llenas, lo que permitió anotar una carrera. Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo de un toque que impulsó una carrera, un pase fallido permitió que Heliot Ramos anotara y Lombard conectó un sencillo de dos carreras por el centro para poner el 5-0 en el marcador.
No fue un solo golpe fulminante. Fueron nueve bateadores que obligaron a un ex All-Star a lanzar 45 veces en la primera entrada. Esa paciencia es el tipo de ataque que más necesitarán los Yankees en octubre, cuando la ausencia de Judge convierta cada remontada en un esfuerzo colectivo.
Cole se recompone y luego hace historia
La ventaja le permitió a Gerrit Cole respirar tranquilo. El lanzador diestro había encajado siete jonrones en sus dos últimas salidas, y se habían intensificado los rumores sobre si estaría listo para octubre. Con esta actuación, acalló gran parte de esos rumores.
Cole encajó un jonrón de dos carreras de Corbin Carroll en la segunda entrada, de nuevo con una bola rápida que se quedó en el plato, pero nada más. Lanzó seis entradas, cedió dos carreras con cuatro hits, no concedió ninguna base por bolas y ponchó a seis con 90 lanzamientos. Boone había dicho antes del partido que Cole sería el abridor en la serie de comodín de todas formas.
Cole se tomó esta salida como un paso adelante, no como una solución definitiva. Explicó que había dedicado el tiempo entre sus salidas a afinar su lanzamiento para mejorar su capacidad de engaño.
«No creo que lo hayamos hecho perfecto esta noche, pero sí que hemos dado un paso en la dirección correcta», dijo Cole. «Creo que todavía nos queda mucho por hacer. No es fácil, pero es necesario. Así son las grandes ligas».
Esta victoria fue la número 162 de la carrera de Cole, lo que le permitió superar a Mike Moore como el lanzador con más victorias de todos los tiempos entre los elegidos en primera posición en el draft de la MLB, un hito discreto en una noche llena de otros titulares.
Un error defensivo que se corrigió al instante
Esta es la jugada que da forma a la noche, y en la que pocos se fijarán. El error de Lombard dos días antes en Minnesota había formado parte de una secuencia decisiva que le costó a los Yankees un partido que podían haber ganado. El viernes se presentó algo que el deporte rara vez concede tan rápido: una segunda oportunidad sin condiciones.
Su jonrón en la sexta entrada sacó a Rodríguez del partido y amplió la ventaja a 7-2. Para un novato que se vio obligado a ocupar el puesto de campocorto en la recta final, su reacción importó más que las carreras. Cuando le preguntaron por la noche, Lombard lo dejó claro.
«Fue genial desde el principio, todos hicimos buenos turnos al bate», dijo Lombard. «Obviamente, había un buen lanzador en el montículo. Le hicimos trabajar».
Esta actuación llega justo cuando los Yankees están valorando los roles para la postemporada en el cuadro, donde la solidez de un novato ahora tiene un peso real de cara a octubre.
Rice se acerca a los 40 mientras Judge se queda en el banquillo
Rice le dio a los Yankees otro pilar. Su jonrón en la tercera entrada contra Rodríguez recorrió 390 pies y fue el número 39 de la temporada, una cifra que, según el entrenador Aaron Boone, ya había predicho en los entrenamientos de primavera. Rice terminó con ese jonrón y un triple, y suma cinco jonrones en sus últimos 22 partidos.
El ambiente en torno a ese swing era sombrío. Judge había impulsado tantas primeras entradas a lo largo de los años, y ahora los Yankees tienen que volver a luchar por llegar a octubre sin él. Rice se refirió a lo difícil que resulta este momento.
«Es un duro golpe para nosotros», dijo Rice. «Llevábamos mucho tiempo echándole de menos, así que esto nos cuesta especialmente aceptarlo. Pero no nos queda más remedio que seguir jugando a tope y seguir haciendo lo nuestro».
Los Yankees creen que el pitcheo les llevará a la victoria pase lo que pase. Cam Schlittler, el probable ganador del Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, está previsto que sea el abridor en un posible primer partido de la ronda de comodines, con Max Fried y Carlos Rodón como relevos.
Nueva York y Arizona vuelven a enfrentarse este sábado, con Schlittler listo para medirse a Brandon Pfaadt. La inminente serie de cuatro partidos contra los Rays en el Yankee Stadium, que empieza el martes con una doble jornada, podría decidir el título de la división. Por una noche, un novato algo desconcertado y un as que se mantuvo firme hicieron que los Yankees parecieran listos.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.content:encoded:
MLB Trade Rumors | Darragh McDonald: Well, it was nice while it lasted. The Yankees announced yesterday evening that they will be placing right fielder Aaron Judge on the ten-day injured list with a calf strain today; Max Schuemann is expected to be the corresponding move. Since it will be backdated to the 16th, Judge will be eligible to come off the IL for the final day of the season; however, given the nature of calf strains, it is entirely possible that we have seen the last of No. 99 for 2026.
New York Daily News | Gary Phillips: Arguably the biggest surprise of the 2026 season — beyond the fact that the Yankees somehow managed to keep their heads above water despite Aaron Judge missing three months, of course — has been the breakout of outfielder Spencer Jones. The former top prospect has managed to position himself as “a key cog in the Yankees’ lineup,” taking advantage of opportunities offered by injuries to Judge, Trent Grisham, Cody Bellinger, and Giancarlo Stanton. In particular, his performance against southpaws, which had long been a weakness throughout his minor league career, has been a pleasant surprise. That being said, it hasn’t been all sunshine and roses: Jones has yet to flash the leather in the way many have expected him to. Even so, however, it seems likely that Jones will be a critical part of the team’s postseason run, whether as the starting center fielder or a key reserve.
MLB.com | Mike Lupica: For all the attention that the Yankees’ veteran stars — Judge, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, and Giancarlo Stanton — receive, the 2026 season has been a veritable youth movement. Key to that has been the development, of course, of first baseman/designated hitter Ben Rice and AL Cy Young frontrunner Cam Schlittler. The two youngsters from Massachusetts, never highly rated as prospects, have turned themselves into veritable forces at the plate and on the mound, and without their contributions, the injury-riddled 2026 Yankees would almost certainly be spending the final few days of the season playing out the string, not attempting to make a last-ditch run at the AL East while lining up the rotation for a matchup with the Red Sox in the Wild Card round.
MLB Trade Rumors | Darragh McDonald: Yesterday afternoon, the Yankees announced that Oswaldo Cabrera, the popular utilityman who has been with the organization since 2015, had been claimed off waivers by the Cincinnati Reds. He had been designated for assignment earlier in the week, in order to make room on the 40-man roster for Clarke Schmidt.
Playbill | Logan Culwell-Block: Earlier this summer, former Mets infielder José Iglesias made the jump from the ballfield to the stage, joining the Broadway production of Buena Vista Social Club. Now, a Yankee great will be joining him: yesterday, Bernie Williams announced that he will be joining the show’s pit band for a limited run, from October 22nd through November 29th.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX - Gerrit Cole nunca había permitido siete jonrones en un lapso de dos aperturas antes de sus salidas más recientes y, con los playoffs a la vuelta de la esquina, existía la preocupación de que el lanzador derecho de los Yankees hubiera sufrido un bajón de rendimiento.
La mayor parte de esa inquietud provenía de fuera del vestuario. El manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone, afirmó el viernes que se esperaba que Cole abriera un partido si su equipo llegaba a la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana, y el veterano cumplió su promesa de solucionar el problema de los cuadrangulares y lanzó bien en la victoria por 9-2 sobre los Diamondbacks en el Chase Field el viernes por la noche.
Los Yankees (89-64) ganaron por 11ma vez en 15 partidos, colocándose a cuatro juegos de los Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana después de que Tampa Bay perdiera ante Boston más temprano esa misma noche.
Horas después de que Cody Bellinger dijera que los Yankees tendrían que "apoyarse mutuamente" para superar la ausencia de Aaron Judge —quien, tras ganar tres veces el premio al Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana, podría perderse el resto de la temporada regular debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha—, los "Bombarderos" respaldaron a Cole con una primera entrada de cinco carreras.
Cada uno de los primeros cinco bateadores se embasó y anotó ante el venzolano Eduardo Rodríguez. Ben Rice negoció una base por bolas con las bases llenas, el dominicano Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo productor y George Lombard Jr. disparó un sencillo de dos carreras; esto fue parte de una noche de tres carreras impulsadas para el novato, quien también conectó un jonrón en la sexta entrada que provocó la salida de Rodríguez del juego.
Rice también conectó su 39no jonrón —líder del equipo— para apoyar a Cole, quien había permitido jonrones al primer bateador en sus dos aperturas anteriores. Tras dedicar tiempo a ajustar su mecánica de lanzamiento y corregir posibles problemas de revelación de pitcheos desde su última salida contra los Mets, Cole retiró a los bateadores de Arizona en orden durante una primera entrada de 12 lanzamientos.
Corbin Carroll conectó un jonrón de dos carreras ante Cole en la segunda entrada, pero eso fue todo lo que lograron los D-backs. Con un total de 90 lanzamientos (62 strikes), Cole permitió cuatro imparables, no otorgó bases por bolas y ponchó a seis bateadores.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Yankees ride five-run first to series-opening romp of Diamondbacks
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: The two starting pitchers entered this game trending in opposite directions. Gerrit Cole had just allowed the most home runs (seven) in a two-start span in his career, while Eduardo Rodriguez is in the midst of a career year with a 2.62 ERA. One of those trends remained — Cole giving up another home run on a fastball — but fortunately the other trend was momentarily halted, the Yankees scoring five in the first off E-Rod to give themselves enough of a cushion to weather Cole’s continued home run
item.content:encoded:
The two starting pitchers entered this game trending in opposite directions. Gerrit Cole had just allowed the most home runs (seven) in a two-start span in his career, while Eduardo Rodriguez is in the midst of a career year with a 2.62 ERA. One of those trends remained — Cole giving up another home run on a fastball — but fortunately the other trend was momentarily halted, the Yankees scoring five in the first off E-Rod to give themselves enough of a cushion to weather Cole’s continued home run woes.
Cole settled down after the Carroll dinger to give the Yankees six innings, by which time the offense all but put this game out of reach. They kept the pressure on, scoring a further four runs including solo home runs by Ben Rice and George Lombard Jr., to cruise to a series-opening victory in the desert, 9-2.
Rodriguez came into this game with an ERA above six in the first inning and an ERA right around two for the subsequent innings combined. That made it imperative that the Yankees find a way to do damage before the home team had a chance to come to bat, especially with the rate Cole is giving up the long ball. They did just that with a clear disciplined approach not to expand the zone against E-Rod’s curveball.
Paul Goldschmidt drew a leadoff walk, Cody Bellinger followed with a single, and Heliot Ramos also walked to load the bases with no outs. Rice drew the Yankees’ third walk in the first four batters to plate Goldschmidt and open the scoring, Goldy, Ramos, and Rice all working full counts before taking the free pass. Amed Rosario then fought off a cutter that handcuffed him up and in, muscling it to the opposite field perfectly between center and left fielder to plate Bellinger as the runners went station to station. A wild pitch allowed Ramos to score and Rice and Rosario to move up to second and third. This set up a two-run ground ball single from Lombard that just got by Geraldo Perdomo’s diving attempt to atone for his defensive misplay in the 13th that allowed the Twins to walk off the Yankees on Wednesday.
Rodriguez struck out Volpe to end the inning giving him three strikeouts in the frame, but the damage was done. The 45 pitches he threw were the most he’s thrown in the first inning in his career. 33 of those pitches fell out of the zone, but only eight induced a chase.
It’s a good thing they hung such a crooked number, because Cole immediately gave two of those runs back. He gave up a leadoff single to Perdomo before yanking an 0-1 four-seamer right into Corbin Carroll’s nitro zone, the three-time All-Star obliterating it to right for a two-run bomb to reduce the Yankees’ lead, 5-2. Rice made sure to immediately tilt the momentum back in his team’s favor. After falling behind 0-2, he stayed back on an elevated heater from E-Rod riding it out the other way and over the fence in left-center for a leadoff bomb, his 39th of the year, to give Cole some more of his cushion back, 6-2.
Cole settled down to work a scoreless third and fourth, helped in part by a sharp uptick in slider usage at the expense of some four-seamers as well as an impressive sliding catch in left-center by Spencer Jones in the third. He finally began dialing the fastball command to the corners in the fifth, striking out Tim Tawa and Lars Nootbaar on four-seamers to end the frame after Jesús Sánchez singled with one out. This allowed Lombard to restore the Yankees’ five run lead in the sixth, the rookie punishing a hanging curveball from E-Rod by lining the solo shot down the line it left and into the bullpen for his fourth of the year and third RBI on the night.
The four-seamer was the prime culprit for Cole in his previous two starts with a 68.2-percent hard-hit rate and just six whiffs, and that remained the case tonight. However, I believe it is Cole’s rustiness with his secondaries that is leading his four-seamer to get barreled. The fastball still has plenty of velocity — at 97 mph it’s a full tick above last season. I will grant that he has missed location in the zone on numerous occasions which hasn’t done him any favors.
However, after his last start, Cole identified a lack of chase and whiff against his secondaries as the reason his fastball is getting crushed. Hitters being able to lay off those chase pitches forces Cole to overuse the fastball in counts that favor the softer stuff, which in essence gives them the opportunity to hunt the heater when they should be defending against the breaker. When you can hunt a fastball in any count, chances are you are going to do damage when Cole misses his spot in the zone, the high velocity not much of a weapon when hitters’ bats are preemptively sped up.
Indeed, once he started commanding his slider and knuckle curve to the shadow of the zone in the middle innings, the hard contact against the fastball dried up. Having pitched a strong fifth and sixth and with his pitch count at 90, Boone saw no reason to overextend Cole and ended his night after six with his best innings freshest in mind. He finished night having pitched six innings, allowing two runs on four hits with no walks and six strikeouts.
Despite possessing one of the stingiest bullpens in baseball, the Diamondbacks decided that a five-run deficit in the seventh was too steep to justify using their high leverage arms. So, Zac Gallen made his first career relief appearance, the former All-Star in the midst of am injury-plagued, below-replacement-level campaign. He allowed a leadoff single to Goldschmidt and walked Ramos and Rice — again, both in full counts — to load the bases with one out. Aaron Boone sent out Ryan McMahon to pinch-hit for Rosario, and he hit a sharp grounder to first that Pavin Smith gloved but airmailed the underhand toss to Gallen covering first as all the runners were safe and a run scored on the error. Spencer Jones then appeared to ground into the inning-ending double play, but his hustle out of the box and down the line just beat the throw to pick up an RBI and make it 9-2.
Ryan Yarbrough pitched 1.1 innings in relief of Cole and worked himself into and out of trouble in the seventh. Arizona put runners on second and third as Nolan Arenado singled and Carroll doubled with one out. However, Yarbrough struck out Jose Fernandez and Tawa to strand the pair in scoring position. Rice smoked his fourth triple of the year in the ninth but was stranded at third by a McMahon strikeout. Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil recorded the final five outs of the game without allowing a baserunner to seal the win, 9-2. With the Rays having lost to the Red Sox earlier in the evening, the Yankees’ deficit is back to four games in the division, making that looming four-game set against Tampa in the Bronx even more high stakes.
Cam Schlittler looks to cement his AL Cy Young case tomorrow after Dylan Cease suffered his shortest start of the season on Friday. The Yankees ace will face off against Brandon Pfaadt with a slightly more reasonable game start time. First pitch is scheduled for 8:10 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES.
Yankees rout the D-Backs, 9-2, who's your Player of the Game?
Gerrit Cole pitched 6 innings of 2-run ball. George Lombard Jr. hit a two-run single and a solo homer. Ben Rice raked with a solo homer, triple, and two walks.

item.title: [MLB.com] Steady Cole gets back on track as Yanks pick up a game on Rays
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch

Most of that came from outside the clubhouse. item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Gerrit Cole had never surrendered seven home runs over a two-start span before his most recent outings, and with the playoffs around the corner, there was concern that the Yankees’ right-hander might have hit a wall.
Most of that came from outside the clubhouse. Yankees manager Aaron Boone affirmed Friday that Cole should expect to draw a start if his team lands in the American League Wild Card Series, and the veteran made good on his promise to fix the long-ball issue, pitching well in a 9-2 victory over the Diamondbacks at Chase Field on Friday night.
Hours after Cody Bellinger said the Yankees would have to “lean on each other” to overcome Aaron Judge’s absence, with the three-time AL MVP potentially set to miss the rest of the regular season with a right calf strain, the Bombers supported Cole with a five-run first inning.
Each of the first five batters reached base and scored against Eduardo Rodriguez. Ben Rice worked a bases-loaded walk, Amed Rosario lifted a run-scoring single and George Lombard Jr. stroked a two-run single -- part of a three-RBI night for the rookie, who launched a sixth-inning homer that chased Rodriguez.
Rice also slugged his team-leading 39th home run to support Cole, who had served up leadoff homers in his previous two starts. Having spent time focusing on his delivery and potential pitch-tipping issues since his last outing against the Mets, Cole set Arizona down in order during a 12-pitch first inning.
Corbin Carroll cracked a two-run homer in the second inning off Cole, but that was all the D-backs managed. Throwing 90 pitches (62 for strikes), Cole scattered four hits, walking none and striking out six.

item.title: [Yardbarker] New York Yankees Make Spencer Jones Announcement
item.dc:creator: Simeon Kotto
item.description: The New York Yankees open a series in Arizona on Friday night looking to rebound from a one-run loss and find more consistent production from a young outfielder who has shown both power and growing pains. After falling 5-4 to the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday, the club posted its lineup for the first game against the Diamondbacks, and the most notable tweak involved Spencer Jones, via FantasyPros. Jones had occupied the fifth spot in the order against Minnesota and finished without a hit while st
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees open a series in Arizona on Friday night looking to rebound from a one-run loss and find more consistent production from a young outfielder who has shown both power and growing pains.
After falling 5-4 to the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday, the club posted its lineup for the first game against the Diamondbacks, and the most notable tweak involved Spencer Jones, via FantasyPros.
Jones had occupied the fifth spot in the order against Minnesota and finished without a hit while striking out five times. That performance prompted manager Aaron Boone to slide the 25-year-old down one place, into the sixth hole, for Friday’s contest.
The rest of the order features Paul Goldschmidt at first, Cody Bellinger in left, Heliot Ramos in right, Ben Rice as the designated hitter, Amed Rosario at third, George Lombard at short, Austin Wells behind the plate and Anthony Volpe at second. Jones will patrol center field.
The adjustment is modest on paper, yet it reflects the reality of a rookie season that has mixed encouraging numbers with stretches of swing-and-miss. Jones is hitting .252 with 59 hits, 10 home runs, 37 RBIs, 32 runs and nine stolen bases across 79 games.
Those totals represent real production for a player who made his major-league debut earlier this year after being selected in the first round of the 2022 draft out of Vanderbilt.
At 6-foot-7, 240 pounds, he possesses the kind of raw power that can change a game in a single swing, something he demonstrated with a three-run homer against the Twins just a few days earlier.
Still, five strikeouts in one night is the kind of night that forces a lineup shuffle. Boone has moved Jones around the order several times this season as the Yankees try to maximize his strengths while limiting damage against certain pitching looks.
The Diamondbacks series offers another chance to see whether a slightly lower spot in the batting order helps him settle in and put the ball in play more often.
New York arrives in Phoenix needing wins as the calendar moves deeper into September. A tight loss in Minnesota left little margin, and every at-bat from a developing bat like Jones carries extra weight.
The organization drafted him for his combination of size, athleticism and power; the challenge now is translating that package into more consistent contact at the highest level.
Friday’s lineup is a small tactical step in that process rather than a dramatic demotion.
Whether Jones responds with extra-base hits or continues to chase pitches remains to be seen. What is clear is that the Yankees still view him as part of their present and future outfield mix.
A drop from fifth to sixth is not a verdict on his season. It is simply the latest attempt to put a young player in a position where his next good swing can matter.

A fun weekend in prospect at Chase – at least, outside the lines, where the team will be celebrating the 25th anniversary of their World Series win against these same Yankees. The main party is taking place tomorrow night, but there are some things to note for tonight. Most relevantly to me who is recapping: Greg Schulte, the voice of the D-backs from their first Opening Day in 1998, through the end of the 2023 World Series, is making a return to the booth tonight. I've no idea how the sync between that and the TV broadcast will work out, but I think I am prepared to handle a little bit of lag for the evening.
With it being Friday night, and since I'm being robbed of most of my usual Friday night entertainment for recappage purposes – no eighties DJ on Twitch, no B-movie about killer hippopotami (they missed a trick by not calling the latter, Hippocalypse Now) – I will once again be tucking into my cider selection. Worked out well enough last Friday night, if my (slightly blurry) recollections are anything to go by. I think I have one untried flavor from the selection pack, plus a couple of "regular" brands in the fridge. You have been warned. Tim should be back for the final series next weekend, both you and my liver will be pleased to hear. 🙂
Another narrative will be taking the first pitch of the game, with Paul Goldschmidt returning to Chase Field. I'm sure he'll still get a warm welcome, even though he is now 1,104 games (including the post-season) removed from the last time Goldy pulled on the Sedona Red. I was looked at the 2018 roster, and there aren't many people there who are still playing in the majors this season. Ketel Marte, obviously – he was the "baby" of the roster that year! – and Ildemaro Vargas, then still a rookie. A few starting pitchers, in Taijuan Walker, Robbie Ray and Patrick Corbin. That's about it, on a quick, non-structured glance. Let me know if I missed any!

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Anthony Volpe Handed Harsh Take on New York Yankees Future Before Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Cole Shelton
item.description: The New York Yankees could make a surprising move on Anthony Volpe. Volpe has had success since being recalled, but George Lombard Jr. has taken over as the starting shortstop. So, Volpe's future in New York is very much up in the air. New York will begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday. New York Yankees Surprise Anthony Volpe Decision Although Volpe has been playing better, he isn't guaranteed a spot on the Yankees playoff roster. After New York clinched a pl
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could make a surprising move on Anthony Volpe.
Volpe has had success since being recalled, but George Lombard Jr. has taken over as the starting shortstop. So, Volpe's future in New York is very much up in the air.
New York will begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday.
New York Yankees Surprise Anthony Volpe Decision
Although Volpe has been playing better, he isn't guaranteed a spot on the Yankees playoff roster.
After New York clinched a playoff spot, Yankees analysts Bryan Hoch and Patrick Donnelly of MLB.com revealed the likely playoff roster, and they didn't have Volpe on it.
What could the postseason roster look like?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones, Aaron Judge, Heliot Ramos
DH: Ben Rice
SP: Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole
RP: David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, Tim Hill, Ryan Yarbrough, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, Ryan Weathers, Will Warren
The Yankees leaving Volpe off the playoff roster would be a disappointing outcome for the shortstop. It also could signal the end of his tenure in New York as Lombard is the shortstop of the future.
Volpe is hitting .253 with 2 home runs and 26 RBIs this season with the Yankees.
New York Right Now
The Yankees have clinched a playoff spot as New York will be hosting a Wild Card series again.
"Every year you go through a lot, it seems like. But we've been through a lot this year with injuries, with adversity," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "But credit to them for coming together. Through all the ups and downs, they've been a together group. I feel like they've developed a lot of grit over the season."
However, despite clinching a playoff spot, the Yankees made it clear the job isn't finished. New York likely won't win the AL East again, which is frustrating, but the Yankees have confidence they can go on a deep playoff run.
The Yankees are 88-64 and 5 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the top spot in the AL East.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Anthony Volpe Handed Harsh Take on New York Yankees Future Before Playoffs appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees' Aaron Judge Dilemma Features a Problem No One is Discussing
item.dc:creator: Matthew Schmidt
item.description: New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge returned from a rib stress fracture on Sept. 8, and it took him all of seven games to get injured again. Judge left Wednesday's loss to the Minnesota Twins as a result of what he and the team are calling a "lower leg injury," which almost surely means a calf issue. There have been no definitive updates on his status since, and it's looking more and more like Judge will not play against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night. The playoffs start on Sept. 2
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge returned from a rib stress fracture on Sept. 8, and it took him all of seven games to get injured again.
Judge left Wednesday's loss to the Minnesota Twins as a result of what he and the team are calling a "lower leg injury," which almost surely means a calf issue.
There have been no definitive updates on his status since, and it's looking more and more like Judge will not play against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night.
The playoffs start on Sept. 29, which obviously creates a nightmare scenario for the Yankees. Even if Judge is healthy enough to play.
Why? Because at this point, the three-time AL MVP pretty much has to serve as a designated hitter. Unless Judge has a minor bruise in his calf, it seems highly unlikely that he will be able to play right field if he returns.
Why is that a big deal? Because it completely messes up New York's lineup.
The Yankees acquired Luis Garcia Jr. back at the MLB trade deadline with the expectation that he would be the first baseman. Ben Rice would then serve as DH, as Giancarlo Stanton's status was up in the air then, and now, it looks like Stanton is done for the year.
When Judge is in right field, that isn't an issue. Garcia plays first, Rice goes to DH and all three of those big boppers are in the lineup.
But with Judge potentially having to spend all of his time at designated hitter, that means Garcia would almost certainly get the boot.
You're not platooning Rice and Garcia at first. They're both lefties, and you always want Rice's bat in the lineup no matter what. What the Yankees could have done was platoon Garcia and Paul Goldschmidt at first base given how much Goldschmidt mashes lefties, but if Judge is DHing, that isn't possible.
If Judge is healthy enough to hit, he'll obviously be in the lineup. Running the bases could be another story (just ask Giancarlo), but the more you limit Judge's movement, the better.
That the Yankees have been so mum on Judge's status is concerning. If there weren't a major problem here, they surely would have already said something.
And after all of the experience fans have had with the medical stuff and how New York handles injuries, they know by now that when there is silence, there is reason to worry.
Hopefully, Judge's malady is no big deal and he can head back out to right field within the next week. But Yankees fans need to prepare for other scenarios, and even if Judge does return, that could mean their lineup still wouldn't be all it could be,

item.title: [MLB.com] ¿Cómo responderán los jóvenes de Yankees en los playoffs?
item.dc:creator: Patrick Donnelly
item.description: Es común pensar en los Yankees como un equipo experimentado en los playoffs. Después de todo, ésta es la octava vez en nueve años que han llegado a la postemporada bajo la dirección del manager Aaron Boone. Y una rápida mirada a algunos de sus jugadores principales muestra una alineación que varía entre un poco y una gran cantidad de experiencia en octubre. Jugador, Número de Partidos de Playoffs de por vida Cody Bellinger, 76 Aaron Judge, 65 Paul Goldschmidt, 29 Trent Grisham, 26 Jazz Chisholm,
item.content:encoded:
Es común pensar en los Yankees como un equipo experimentado en los playoffs. Después de todo, ésta es la octava vez en nueve años que han llegado a la postemporada bajo la dirección del manager Aaron Boone. Y una rápida mirada a algunos de sus jugadores principales muestra una alineación que varía entre un poco y una gran cantidad de experiencia en octubre.
Jugador, Número de Partidos de Playoffs de por vida
Cody Bellinger, 76
Aaron Judge, 65
Paul Goldschmidt, 29
Trent Grisham, 26
Jazz Chisholm, Jr. 24
Austin Wells, 21
Anthony Volpe, 21
Amed Rosario, 11
Ryan McMahon, 10
Ben Rice, 6
José Caballero, 3
Pero faltan algunos nombres en esa lista: El campocorto George Lombard Jr., el jardinero Spencer Jones, el primera base dominicano Luis García Jr. y el jardinero puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos. Ninguno de esos cuatro nunca ha jugado en la postemporada, ya sea con los Yankees o, como es el caso de García y Ramos, con sus equipos anteriores.
Ahora, es posible que algunos de los jugadores veteranos lesionados -- Grisham y Chisholm, específicamente -- puedan regresar a la alineación y enviar a algunos de esos nuevos rostros a la banca o fuera del roster de postemporada por completo. Pero es seguro decir que los Yankees van a contar con al menos algunos novatos en los playoffs el próximo mes, en su búsqueda de ganar su primera Serie Mundial desde el 2009.
Boone ha expresado que sus jóvenes y los recién llegados a los playoffs tienen otra ventaja sobre los jugadores en otros mercados.
"Jugar para los Yankees, jugar en Nueva York”, dijo, "tiene una manera de prepararte para la postemporada”.
Éste ha sido un año de transición en las Grandes Ligas. Consulta la primera ronda del Draft del 2023 si quieres pruebas. No menos de 19 de las 37 selecciones de primera ronda y de compensación han debutado en las Mayores, y muchos de ellos ya son jugadores clave en sus equipos.
"Los jugadores están llegando a las Grandes Ligas a un ritmo muy rápido ahora y a temprana edad”, manifestó el piloto de los Tigers, A.J. Hinch, quien ha dado la bienvenida a la tercera selección Max Clark y al favorito para Novato del Año de la Liga Americana, Kevin McGonigle, a Detroit este año. "No creo que se sientan tan impresionados por los grandes pasos que están dando”.
Para los Yankees, ese grupo incluye a Lombard, quien se ha aclimatado bien desde que fue subido a principios de agosto. Y Jones fue elogiado recientemente nada menos que por Aaron Judge, quien dijo que el jardinero novato "realmente ha evolucionado cada vez que ha sido subido, mejorando un poco más en cada ocasión”.
Por supuesto, habrá contratiempos en el camino. El miércoles, Jones se fue de 6-0 con cinco ponches y cometió un error cuando dejó caer un batazo en el jardín central. Y Lombard no pudo atrapar un roletazo del boricua Victor Caratini en la 13ª entrada que fue considerado un sencillo mientras los Mellizos vencían a los Yankees.
Pero cualquiera que siga el béisbol sabe que los días malos y las malas jugadas son parte del ciclo de crecimiento de un jugador de Grandes Ligas. La clave es aprender de ellos para poder limitarlos en el futuro. Y todo ello -- lo bueno, lo malo y lo ocasionalmente feo -- ayuda a preparar a un joven jugador para su primera vez jugando en el béisbol de octubre.
El mundo está a punto de descubrir lo preparados que están los Yankees jóvenes. Pero Jones ofreció un poco de tranquilidad el lunes mientras disfrutaba de la celebración en el vestuario después de la victoria en Target Field que aseguró otra clasificación de Nueva York para los playoffs.
"Creo que para nosotros, jugamos mejor cuando la multitud se vuelve más ruidosa", dijo. "Estoy bien emocionado por lo que está por venir”.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Cody Bellinger Soluciona Un Problema Clave De Los Yankees Que Lastraba Su Alineación Para La Serie Mundial De 2024
item.dc:creator: Esteban Quiñones
item.description: NUEVA YORK — La diferencia de tres puntos de Cody Bellinger en el platoon le da a los Yankees una gran ventaja en la alineación para la postemporada de octubre. La clasificación sigue siendo importante. Y también lo es una alineación que tendrá poco margen de error cua
item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK — La diferencia de tres puntos de Cody Bellinger en el platoon le da a los Yankees una gran ventaja en la alineación para la postemporada de octubre.
Con un balance de 88-64, los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero siguen a cinco partidos de los Tampa Bay Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana, cuando quedan 10 partidos de la temporada regular. La clasificación sigue siendo importante. Y también lo es una alineación que tendrá poco margen de error cuando los rivales puedan adaptar sus estrategias de pitcheo para contrarrestarla.
Ahí es donde la postemporada de 2024 sigue siendo un contexto útil. Nueva York llegó a la Serie Mundial antes de caer ante los Dodgers en cinco partidos, pero el jardín izquierdo nunca llegó a ser una fuente fiable de producción tanto ofensiva como defensiva. Alex Verdugo terminó esa temporada regular con un promedio de .233/.291/.356 y un OPS+ de 83, y luego bateó .208/.309/.313 con un OPS de .622 en 14 partidos de postemporada.
El problema duró más de un mes de octubre. Tras la última temporada de Brett Gardner con los Yankees en 2021, el jardín izquierdo pasó a ser una posición rotativa en lugar de un punto fuerte consolidado. Las estadísticas posicionales de FanGraphs sitúan al jardín izquierdo de los Yankees en solo 1,6 fWAR entre 2021 y 2024, lo que lo coloca en el puesto 28 de las Grandes Ligas en ese periodo. Esa trayectoria dejó a Nueva York buscando tanto rendimiento como estabilidad, en lugar de otro parche de una sola temporada en una posición defensiva clave. Por fin, la situación parece haber cambiado.
Bellinger convierte el jardín izquierdo de un compromiso en un punto fuerte
Cody Bellinger es la razón más clara. El miércoles conectó 3 de 5, con una base por bolas, una carrera y una base robada, lo que le ha permitido sumar varios hits en cinco de sus últimos siete partidos. Su racha va más allá de unas cuantas noches de septiembre.
Bellinger ha bateado .340 con cinco jonrones, 18 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 148 en 23 partidos desde que volvió el 23 de agosto tras una distensión de grado 2 en el isquiotibial izquierdo. Al comenzar el viernes, llevaba un promedio de bateo de .276/.351/.444, con 16 jonrones y 71 carreras impulsadas en 125 partidos.
Los Yankees acabaron con un balance de 15-7 en los primeros 22 partidos tras su regreso, batearon .274/.336/.440 como equipo, registraron un diferencial de carreras de +42 y anotaron al menos cinco carreras en 14 ocasiones. Llegaron a las seis carreras en 12 ocasiones y a las siete en nueve. Bellinger ha aportado toda esa potencia ofensiva sin dejar de ser un defensor decisivo.
Sports Info Solutions le atribuye a Bellinger 20 carreras defensivas salvadas en el jardín izquierdo, mientras que Statcast le da seis outs por encima de la media en todo el jardín. Ese valor en ambos aspectos es la diferencia clave con respecto a 2024, y su capacidad para jugar tanto en el jardín central como en primera base aporta a los Yankees una mayor flexibilidad en la plantilla.
Una derrota aplastante dejó claro por qué su bate es tan importante
Los Yankees pudieron comprobar su poder ofensivo durante la derrota por 12-2 ante los Mets el 12 de septiembre en el Yankee Stadium. Bellinger anotó las dos carreras de Nueva York con un sencillo impulsador en la cuarta entrada y un jonrón solitario en la sexta. Era su tercer jonrón en cuatro partidos en ese momento.
Aaron Boone estaba explicando por qué el lanzador titular de los Mets, Zac Thornton, había controlado al resto de la alineación. Ese comentario ponía de manifiesto lo poco que Cody Bellinger había recibido ayuda aquella tarde.
«Está claro que se puso por delante ahí y sus lanzamientos a la zona de strike fueron realmente buenos», dijo Boone.
Desde entonces, el promedio de bateo de Bellinger en septiembre ha subido hasta el 0,390 en 14 partidos, con cuatro jonrones, 12 carreras impulsadas y 14 carreras anotadas. Los Yankees han necesitado esa estabilidad mientras otras partes de la alineación han tenido que adaptarse a las lesiones y a los enfrentamientos.
Una diferencia de tres puntos en el platoon cambia las cuentas de octubre
Quizá la cifra más reveladora sea la que apenas varía. Hasta el miércoles, Bellinger tiene un OPS de 0,797 contra lanzadores zurdos y un OPS de 0,794 contra lanzadores diestros. Esa diferencia de tres puntos le da a los Yankees un bateador en el centro del orden de bateo que no hace falta ocultar cuando los rivales cambian de lanzador.
El panorama del platooning de los Yankees también sitúa a Aaron Judge y Ben Rice entre sus bateadores titulares más equilibrados. Bellinger es otro bateador que puede quedarse en el partido sin que Boone tenga que sacrificar el ataque por la defensa ni la defensa por el ataque, una cualidad muy valiosa cuando, en octubre, los bullpens cambian los enfrentamientos inning tras inning.
El precio original del traspaso solo cuenta la mitad de la historia
Los Yankees ficharon a Bellinger de los Cubs en diciembre de 2024 a cambio del lanzador diestro Cody Poteet, y Chicago también aportó 5 millones de dólares. El precio de ese traspaso sigue siendo impresionante, pero no es el coste total. Después de que Bellinger se convirtiera en agente libre, Nueva York lo volvió a fichar en enero con un contrato de cinco años y 162,5 millones de dólares.
En 2025, sumó 29 jonrones, 98 carreras impulsadas y 4,9 fWAR. El valor que le da FanGraphs para 2026 ronda ahora los cuatro fWAR. Según un cálculo basado en sus estadísticas totales de la MLB durante las dos temporadas con los Yankees , se sitúa en 45 jonrones, 169 carreras impulsadas y un promedio de bateo combinado de aproximadamente .274/.341/.464.
Con la clasificación para la postemporada asegurada y la División Este de la Liga Americana aún en juego, a los Yankees les quedan 10 partidos para pulir su alineación de octubre. El reciente repunte de Bellinger, su rendimiento casi idéntico en el plato y su defensa en el jardín izquierdo aportan a Nueva York algo que su equipo de la Serie Mundial de 2024 nunca tuvo de forma constante en esa posición: un titular que puede seguir formando parte del plan independientemente del rival.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.title: [MLB.com] Schlittler, Rice more than just most valuable Yanks, they're indispensable
item.dc:creator: Mike Lupica
item.description: The two most valuable Yankees this season are a starting pitcher named Cam Schlittler, from Walpole, Mass., and Northeastern University, a school within walking distance of Fenway Park, and Ben Rice, who comes out of Cohasset, Mass., on the state’s South Shore, about 30 miles from Fenway. If the Yankees are hosting a Wild Card Series against the Red Sox in less than two weeks -- at Yankee Stadium and not Fenway -- Schlittler and Rice will be the biggest reasons. Schlittler ought to win the AL Cy
item.content:encoded:
The two most valuable Yankees this season are a starting pitcher named Cam Schlittler, from Walpole, Mass., and Northeastern University, a school within walking distance of Fenway Park, and Ben Rice, who comes out of Cohasset, Mass., on the state’s South Shore, about 30 miles from Fenway. If the Yankees are hosting a Wild Card Series against the Red Sox in less than two weeks -- at Yankee Stadium and not Fenway -- Schlittler and Rice will be the biggest reasons.
Schlittler ought to win the AL Cy Young Award and ought to be an MVP candidate for the whole league. David Cone, now a Yankees broadcaster for the YES network and once a great Yankee himself, has one word to describe what he’s seen from Schlittler this season:
“Nails.”
Here’s a breakdown of Schlittler’s ERA, month by month after one start in March, when, of course, he threw a shutout (eight strikeouts) into the sixth inning against the Giants:
1.73 in April
1.48 in May
3.38 in June
1.93 in July
2.33 in August
0.86 so far in September
Carlos Rodón got hurt. Max Fried got hurt. Gerrit Cole joined the season late, and he hasn’t looked like his own Cy Young self lately. It is been Schlittler who has been the Yankees' ace, who is their Game 1 guy, who has carried the staff. He is not going to end up with a 25-3 record and an ERA of 1.74 the way Ron Guidry did nearly 50 years ago. But Schlittler is at 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA going into his last few starts of the regular season. He has been the first young power starter out of the Yankees’ system since Guidry to be this good, and this dominant.
But Rice has been just as important to their offense.
In a season when Aaron Judge was gone for more than 80 games because of a fracture to his rib cage. Then, after Judge finally got back into the lineup and even hit his first home run in months, he left a game against the Twins the other day because of pain in his lower leg. It is why you have to believe, if and when Judge is back in the lineup again, he’s going to be a swing and a prayer the rest of the way.
So No. 99 went away. So did Cody Bellinger, the Yankees’ second-most important hitter a year ago, before he finally returned from the IL. But even when the Yankees struggled to score runs, and even in a roller-coaster year that saw Rice hit just .196 in June and .184 in August, it is Rice who has been the Yankees' hitting star, coming into a weekend series against the Diamondbacks with 38 home runs and still with a chance to knock in 100.
Luis García Jr. showed up from the Nationals at the Trade Deadline to give him some backup. Bellinger has been on a heater since coming off the IL, with five homers, 18 RBIs and a .344 average over his last 22 games. But it was Rice around whom the Yankees built what offense they had before all that, while they were staying ahead of the Red Sox and at least maintaining contact with the Rays.
You know how many homegrown Yankees have hit 40 or more home runs in a season in the last 75 years? Two. One was named Mickey Mantle and the other is Judge. There have been other Yankees sluggers who got to 40 and beyond. Alex Rodriguez once made it all the way to 57. But they all came from somewhere else. Rice is the same as Schlittler: He hasn’t just come to this moment from New England, he’s someone the Yankees drafted in the 12th round of the 2021 Draft (Schlittler was out of the seventh round the following year).
Alfonso Soriano made his own run at 40 more than 20 years ago. Did it twice. But Soriano came to the Yankees as a free agent from Japan. So think about the company Rice will be keeping if does get to 40 homers, starting with his chance this weekend against the Diamondbacks:
Mantle. Judge.
Here is something Rice’s manager, Aaron Boone, has said about him:
"I got my first taste of him in Spring Training of '24, and it was like, 'Oh, OK.' But then this year, it's gone to even another level.”
Here is something else:
“I think he's turning into one of the best hitters in the league."
Rice himself has predictably low-keyed what he’s done for the Yankees so far.
"The year is still in progress, you know?” he said. “It's still going on. We've got more games to play and a long road ahead, so I can't really look back and assess it fully yet."
It really has been a roller-coaster ride occasionally. He has struggled occasionally against left-handed pitchers, but his season-long average against them stands at .254 with 10 home runs and 29 RBIs.
We know what Schlittler’s numbers are. Rice’s, though, can get a little lost sometimes. But in a year where he’s batted everywhere from leadoff to cleanup, when Judge was gone for more than half the time, he has been indispensable, too. And still has a shot to be a 40-homer guy for the Yankees.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Aumenta El Temor A Que Aaron Judge Se Convierta En El Villano De Los Yankees En Octubre Tras Su último Contratiempo Por Lesión

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Durante más de tres meses, los Yankees de Nueva York han planificado el regreso de Aaron Judge en torno a una idea: recuperar a su capitán para octubre sin exigirle que recupere de golpe los 99 días que se ha perdido.
Por eso su primera semana tras el regreso nunca pareció normal. Judge volvió sin haber pasado por una etapa de rehabilitación en las ligas menores. Los Yankees limitaron sus entradas, intercalaron descansos programados y consideraron los partidos de las Grandes Ligas como la fase final de su preparación. Solo jugó seis entradas en su regreso el 8 de septiembre y el martes tuvo un descanso programado tras disputar seis partidos seguidos.
Los Yankees estaban dispuestos a sacrificar el ritmo de septiembre a cambio de la forma física en octubre. Para este fin de semana en Arizona, se suponía que esa ecuación iba a cambiar. Judge ya había superado la fase de entrenamiento controlado. Nueva York se preparaba para aumentar su carga de trabajo y darle esos turnos al bate regulares que se había perdido durante su larga recuperación en la liga mayor.
La urgencia ya se notaba en los resultados. Judge tenía un promedio de 4 de 21 con 11 strikeouts en sus primeros seis partidos tras su reincorporación. Su jonrón de tres carreras del lunes en Minnesota fue la primera señal de que estaba dando la talla, pero no borró todos esos swings fallidos. Los Yankees necesitaban más práctica que otro reinicio.
Según la clasificación de la MLB, los Yankees tienen un balance de 88-64 al comenzar el viernes, a cinco partidos del Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, con 10 partidos por disputar. Cuatro de ellos serán contra los Rays la semana que viene. La plaza para la postemporada está asegurada, pero Nueva York todavía tiene que prepararse para la lucha por el título de división y una posible serie de comodines.
Por eso, esta etapa no se centró tanto en demostrar que Judge podía volver, sino más bien en asegurarse de que pudiera volver a asumir la carga de trabajo habitual de octubre. Se suponía que cada partido le acercaría un poco más a su máximo rendimiento, le ayudaría a recuperar la sincronización frente a los lanzadores de las Grandes Ligas y eliminaría otra incertidumbre de cara a la postemporada. Se suponía que esa iba a ser la fase final y sin complicaciones del plan de los Yankees para octubre, antes de que empezara la postemporada.
El plan de puesta en marcha se ve interrumpido
En cambio, Judge llega a Arizona con una molestia en la parte inferior de la pierna derecha tras la derrota del miércoles por 5-4, en la 13.ª entrada, ante los Minnesota Twins en el Target Field. Notó el problema por primera vez en la primera entrada y siguió en el campo hasta que Heliot Ramos entró como bateador suplente en su lugar en la sexta.
Era su séptimo partido desde que volvió tras una fractura por estrés en la costilla derecha, después de 99 días de baja. Con esos dos strikeouts, su promedio desde que volvió queda en 4 de 23, con 13 strikeouts y un jonrón.
Judge dijo que intentó seguir jugando antes de que él y el entrenador Aaron Boone decidieran que el riesgo para los Yankees era mayor que lo que valía seguir en el campo.
«Intenté seguir jugando a ver hasta dónde podía llegar, porque estos partidos son importantes en esta recta final», dijo Judge. «Lo hablé con los míos y pensamos que sería lo mejor para no perjudicar al equipo, ni en el campo ni en las bases».
Los Yankees tuvieron el jueves libre para someterse a tratamiento. A primera hora del viernes, la MLB seguía indicando que tenía una contractura en la parte inferior de la pierna derecha, sin fecha de regreso.
David Cone señala un problema aún mayor para octubre
La primera cuestión es la disponibilidad. La más importante es la preparación.
El analista de YES Network, David Cone, se centró en eso el jueves. Judge ha tenido 24 turnos al bate desde que volvió, y 13 de ellos han acabado en strikeouts.
«Estoy preocupado», dijo Cone. «Necesita turnos al bate… Tiene un problema en la parte inferior de la pierna, en la pantorrilla. Simplemente no lo sabemos. No lo sabremos hasta que sepamos qué tan grave es. ¿Va a tener más turnos al bate antes de que acabe la temporada regular? Ahora mismo es una auténtica incógnita».
Ahora, el hecho de haberse saltado la fase de rehabilitación cobra más importancia. El exreceptor All-Star A.J. Pierzynski dijo que una temporada en las ligas menores podría haberle proporcionado un entorno menos exigente para lidiar con las molestias tras una larga ausencia.
«Por eso te vas de rehabilitación, sobre todo cuando has estado tanto tiempo de baja como Aaron Judge. Él mismo lo ha dicho: esto es como los entrenamientos de primavera, así que intentas quitarte de encima las molestias y otras cosillas que surgen yendo de rehabilitación», dijo Pierzynski. «Él no lo hizo, no quiso hacerlo».
Nadie puede saber si una asignación a la rehabilitación habría evitado esa tensión en la pierna. Los Yankees ahora corren el riesgo de que Judge pierda más turnos al bate que aún necesita.
El equilibrio de los pelotones no es el problema
Una comparación actual del OPS de los Yankees y los Red Sox destaca a Judge, Ben Rice y Cody Bellinger como bateadores de Nueva York que rinden bien contra cualquiera de los dos equipos. Según Baseball Savant, Judge tiene un OPS de 0,839 contra lanzadores diestros y de 0,892 contra zurdos. Bellinger tiene unas cifras casi idénticas: 0,794 y 0,795. Rice tiene un OPS de 0,937 contra lanzadores diestros y de 0,784 contra zurdos.
Judge no necesita un papel de bateador de reserva. Los Yankees necesitan que esté listo para batear regularmente contra cualquier rival.
Judge tiene un promedio de bateo de .241/.360/.511, con 18 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos. La cuestión es si los Yankees podrán recuperar el ritmo de juego suficiente antes de octubre.
El plazo de la Liga Internacional convierte la precaución en una apuesta con la plantilla
Si los Yankees metieran a Judge en la lista de lesionados ahora, no podría jugar hasta el partido 161, lo que le dejaría, como mucho, el último partido de la temporada regular para ponerse a punto.
Si los Yankees creen que puede volver antes, pueden mantenerlo en la plantilla y jugar temporalmente con un jugador menos disponible en la plantilla de 28.
Jasson Domínguez y Max Schuemann figuraban ambos en la alineación del equipo de Triple A de Scranton/Wilkes-Barre el jueves, lo que sugiere que no habrá ningún sustituto inmediato.
Esto deja a Nueva York ante la disyuntiva que intentó evitar durante el primer regreso de Judge: proteger su físico o proteger su preparación. A falta de 10 partidos, puede que los Yankees no tengan tiempo suficiente para hacer ambas cosas a fondo.
¿Qué opinas? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.title: [sports.yahoo.com] Expert Explains Why He Got Yankees’ Ben Rice Wrong
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: Keith Law is one of the most widely respected prospects writers in baseball, and one thing he tries to do is explain why he gets certain players wrong. In a new article on Thursday, he dove into New York Yankees star Ben Rice, whom he never viewed as a high-ranking prospect. Of course, Law was not alone in his assessment. Rice went to Dartmouth, not known as a baseball powerhouse, and he was a 12th-round pick in the 2021 MLB Draft, having missed out on a lot of college baseball because of the CO
item.content:encoded:
Keith Law is one of the most widely respected prospects writers in baseball, and one thing he tries to do is explain why he gets certain players wrong.
In a new article on Thursday, he dove into New York Yankees star Ben Rice, whom he never viewed as a high-ranking prospect.
Of course, Law was not alone in his assessment.
Rice went to Dartmouth, not known as a baseball powerhouse, and he was a 12th-round pick in the 2021 MLB Draft, having missed out on a lot of college baseball because of the COVID-19 pandemic and ending up with just one homer in his college career.
Nothing about Rice's outward pedigree screamed future star.
But through Sept. 16, Rice has belted 38 home runs and driven in 92 runs in the 2026 MLB season. Clearly, he's a star.
The 27-year old lefty slugger just wasn't always seen this way.
What Prospect Rankings Got Wrong
One of the first things that struck Law was that Rice was a catcher who wasn't going to stay a catcher. That's always a negative.
Rice also didn't have an early start in the minor leagues, and so he was always older than most at his level.
"Even when he started producing in the minor leagues, with a 20-homer season across three levels in 2023, he was old for the levels he played at and didn't have a position — he was a catcher with no shot to stay there," Law wrote on Thursday. "His swing was extremely uphill, prioritizing power over everything else, and in his first stint in the majors in 2024, pitchers exploited that swing path, leading to his first struggles in pro ball."
It turns out that Rice kept making the changes and improvements that would help him become a quality big leaguer, though.
"Rice went out that offseason and worked on his swing and his body, gaining enough strength to improve his bat speed and, naturally, his contact quality," Law writes. "It wasn't his first rodeo — he'd changed his stance and swing while in college — but this change was more dramatic, with a much more open setup and a stride that didn't close himself off, helping him roll over to the right side less often and, at least in 2025, pull the ball in the air more. The change also made him less vulnerable on stuff middle-in; in 2024, he whiffed on 25 percent of pitches on the inner third, then cut that to 11.3 percent in 2025 and 11.9 percent so far this year. He's still not a catcher, but he's a top-10 bat in the majors this year."
Keith Law on Cam Schlittler
Law goes on in the same blurb to note that he also never saw Yankees pitching star Cam Schlittler turning out to be this good.
"He barely threw a sinker at all when I saw him, and used it just 6.1 percent of the time in the majors last year, but this year he's used it 19.6 percent of the time," Law writes. "Schlittler has thrown something other than one of his three fastballs just 10.6 percent of the time this year. Only Chad Patrick throws fewer non-fastballs among starters with 100+ innings this year; Misiorowski is fourth on the list at 18.3 percent."
A prospect analyst would want to see more than just a good fastball to be high on a pitcher.
Schlittler's fastball variety pack has turned out to be so good that he's hardly needed anything else, a total outlier but a total star.

item.content:encoded:
Will Yankees' postseason first-timers prove to be ready for the moment?
This browser does not support the video element.
It’s common to think of the Yankees as a playoff-tested team. After all, this is the eighth time in nine years that they’ve made the postseason under manager Aaron Boone. And a quick look at some of their regulars shows a lineup that varies between a little bit and a wealth of October experience.
Player No. of Career Playoff Games
Cody Bellinger 76
Aaron Judge 65
Paul Goldschmidt 29
Trent Grisham 26
Jazz Chisholm, Jr. 24
Austin Wells 21
Anthony Volpe 21
Amed Rosario 11
Ryan McMahon 10
Ben Rice 6
José Caballero 3
But a few names are missing from that list: Shortstop George Lombard Jr., outfielder Spencer Jones, first baseman Luis García Jr. and outfielder Heliot Ramos. Those four have never played in the postseason, either with the Yankees or -- as is the case with García and Ramos -- with their previous teams.
Now, it’s possible that some of the injured veteran players -- Grisham and Chisholm, specifically -- could return to the lineup and send some of those new faces to the bench or off the playoff roster entirely. But it’s safe to say the Yankees are going to be counting on at least a few playoff newbies next month in their quest to win their first World Series since 2009.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said his youngsters and playoff newcomers have another advantage over players who are coming of age in other markets.
“You play for the Yankees, you play in New York,” he said, “it has a way of getting you ready for the postseason.”

But a few names are missing from that list: Shortstop George Lombard Jr., outfielder Spencer Jones, first baseman Luis García Jr. and outfielder Heliot Ramos. Those four have never played in the postseason, either with the Yankees or -- as is the case with García and Ramos -- with their previous teams.
Now, it’s possible that some of the injured veteran players -- Grisham and Chisholm, specifically -- could return to the lineup and send some of those new faces to the bench or off the playoff roster entirely. But it’s safe to say the Yankees are going to be counting on at least a few playoff newbies next month in their quest to win their first World Series since 2009.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said his youngsters and playoff newcomers have another advantage over players who are coming of age in other markets.
“You play for the Yankees, you play in New York,” he said, “it has a way of getting you ready for the postseason.”
This has been something of a transitional year in the Major Leagues. Check out the first round of the 2023 Draft if you want proof. No fewer than 19 of the 37 first-round and sandwich picks have debuted, and many of them are already impact players with their teams.
“Players are getting to the big leagues at a very quick pace now and at a young age,” said Tigers manager A.J. Hinch, who has welcomed No. 3 pick Max Clark and AL Rookie of the Year favorite Kevin McGonigle to Detroit this year. “I don't think they're as wowed by the big steps that they're taking.”
For the Yankees, that class includes Lombard, who has acclimated nicely since being called up in early August. And Jones was recently lauded by none other than Aaron Judge, who said the rookie outfielder has “really evolved every single time he got called up, gotten a little bit better and a little bit better.”
Of course, there will be hiccups along the way. On Wednesday, Jones went 0-for-6 with five strikeouts and committed an error when he dropped a fly ball in center field. And Lombard couldn’t come up with a Victor Caratini grounder in the 13th that was ruled a single as the Twins walked off the Yankees.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees, much like all the other postseason teams in MLB, will have to make tough decisions when it comes to their October roster.
It's a 26-man roster in October across MLB, and no team can carry more than 13 pitchers. How a club opts to round out its roster is entirely up to them, but speaking to the New York Yankees, a recent postseason projection leaves players like Paul Goldschmidt on the fringe.
So, what should the Yankees do with their playoff roster, and who needs to be left off?
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to George Lombard Jr. Blunder in Yankees-Twins Game
Yankees Urged to Dump Paul Goldschmidt from Playoff Roster
In a recent piece for FanSided.com, writer Jake Elman predicts a handful of Yankees players who could be dumped from the postseason roster, and Goldschmidt's name pops up:
"Let's get back to the present. Goldschmidt is hitting just .239 with a .680 OPS in 103 second-half plate appearances, and he's only capable of playing first or DHing. Ben Rice fills both roles, and Cody Bellinger can also play first if needed. The one thing potentially working in Goldschmidt's favor is his .313 average and 1.006 OPS against lefties, but that's not enough to warrant a roster spot in our eyes. Sorry, Goldy. At least you'd finally earn a World Series ring if the Yankees finish the job."
Paul Goldschmidt has been somewhat of a solid contributor for the Yankees this season, playing in 101 games and clubbing 18 home runs and 12 doubles, so his playoff status is certainly up for debate at this moment.
After all, not every team has a lefty masher like Goldy who would certainly be used purely as a platoon.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 2 Roster Moves Before Reds Game
Should Paul Goldschmidt Make the Yankees Playoff Roster?
It's obviously all speculation on behalf of Elman, but he does bring up a big crossroads the Yankees will be at when it comes to a Goldschmidt decision.
The 39-year-old Goldy is also batting .253 this season with an OPS+ of 113, so he's an above-average hitter by 13% in MLB, against both righties and lefties.
Good thing I am not in the position to be making decisions like this, but Yankees fans, comment below what you would do with Paul Goldschmidt this October? And would he be part of your ideal Yankees batting order?
More MLB on Heavy: Chicago Cubs Announce Ian Happ News After Bad Braves Loss

item.content:encoded:
Yankees' Cam Schlittler gets interesting MVP update from ESPN analyst originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees don't have Aaron Judge tearing it up and contending for the AL MVP this season, and while Ben Rice has been great, his odds for the award are slim due to his lackluster value defensively.
But that doesn't mean the Yankees don't have someone in contention for the AL MVP award. ESPN analyst Bradford Doolittle does have an advanced statistic that has placed Cam Schlittler near the top of the MVP standings.
While it might still be a long shot for Schlittler to win the AL MVP, Doolittle's "AXE" rating has Schlittler second only to Yordan Alvarez, and not by much, in the AL MVP race.
Cam Schlittler is currently No. 2 in the MVP ranking by an ESPN analyst
"Front-runner: Yordan Alvarez, Houston Astros (146.9 AXE). Next nine: 2, Cam Schlittler, New York Yankees (143.0)," Doolittle writes.
While Doolittle noted that Schlittler has an "uphill battle" to winning the AL MVP, it's not completely out of the question just yet.
With a lack of a true runaway favorite in the AL MVP race, even with Alvarez contending for the AL Triple Crown, Schlittler's chances are much better than they normally might be.
He's been dominant this season and is the favorite, according to Doolittle, to win the AL Cy Young Award. The MVP award is significantly more difficult for Schlittler to win, and it'd take a near-perfect set of circumstances for him to have a chance at this honor.
In 31 starts this season, Schlittler has a 1.95 ERA and 7.1 bWAR. To win the AL MVP, he'd need to make at least one more start, likely a lengthy one without allowing a run, and to take the MLB ERA title, not just the AL ERA title.
Even if he were to pitch a perfect game in his final start of the year, he would need two other things to happen to win this AL MVP award.
The first would be for Alvarez to lose the Triple Crown while the Astros miss out on the playoffs. The other would be for Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays to have a terrible final few games of the year and drop the Rays out of the AL East lead.
All in all, it's nearly impossible for Schlittler to end the 2026 season as the AL MVP. But considering that pitchers never have a chance for this award, the fact that Doolittle is even willing to name him as a candidate is a testament to how great he's been this season.

item.title: [FanSided] Yankees who clinched a playoff spot but could be dumped from the postseason roster

item.content:encoded:
For their sake, the New York Yankees better hope that superstar outfielder Aaron Judge’s newest injury is only a minor setback.
Judge left Wednesday’s extra-inning loss to the Twins with lower leg tightness, immediately raising concerns among fans that he’ll miss the Yankees’ first playoff series. New York entered play on Sept. 17 in firm control of the AL’s top Wild Card seed, putting them on track to host the No. 5 Red Sox in the first round.
If Judge can’t go when the playoffs begin on Sept. 29, then he won’t be the only notable contributor not in uniform during the Wild Card Series. Each team gets 26 players for their playoff rosters, but no more than 13 pitchers. Some clubs opt for 14 position players and 12 pitchers, though we personally prefer a 13-and-13 balance. Additionally, teams can adjust their rosters between series, and obviously they can replace an injured player if needed.
For this list, we’re only including players who are healthy and active as of Sept. 17. In other words, that means Trent Grisham, Giancarlo Stanton, and Ryan Weathers are among those who didn’t qualify. We’ve also omitted Judge because the Yankees haven’t announced the severity of his left leg injury.
Jasson Domínguez, OF
The writing has long been on the wall for Domínguez, who was recently demoted to Triple-A amid another disappointing season. Even if Judge potentially misses the Wild Card Round, it’s difficult to envision the 23-year-old Domínguez returning as a backup outfielder.
Frankly, the entire situation is unfortunate, because neither Domínguez’s talent nor his work ethic has been the issue. He’s always earned rave reviews for his maturity and overall attitude, but injuries — most notably to his elbow and shoulder — have seemingly sapped him of his once-potent power stroke.
Luis Gil, P
Gil has had an odd career, winning AL Rookie of the Year in 2024 despite debuting three years earlier. Injuries have limited him to a 3.92 ERA over 80.1 innings since the start of 2025, and he recently moved to the bullpen. We’ll see whether the Yankees view the 28-year-old as a long-term reliever, or if they’d bring him to spring training as a starter.
But for now, Gil is on the roster bubble, and we don’t expect him to crack the 26-man playoff squad. Clarke Schmidt’s return gives the Yankees another depth arm, and Gil hasn’t shown that he’s worth carrying on a limited staff. That said, we imagine he’d be among the first names called if injuries strike his teammates.
Paul Goldschmidt, 1B/DH
Goldschmidt turned 39 last week, and it’s unclear whether he’s in the final weeks of a likely Hall of Fame career. He’s totaled 65.3 bWAR, and the majority of the 142 players above him are already in the Hall of Fame or will be when they’re eligible.
Let’s get back to the present. Goldschmidt is hitting just .239 with a .680 OPS in 103 second-half plate appearances, and he’s only capable of playing first or DHing. Ben Rice fills both roles, and Cody Bellinger can also play first if needed.
The one thing potentially working in Goldschmidt’s favor is his .313 average and 1.006 OPS against lefties, but that’s not enough to warrant a roster spot in our eyes. Sorry, Goldy. At least you’d finally earn a World Series ring if the Yankees finish the job.
Will Warren, SP
This might come as a surprise, given that we included Warren in our most recent playoff roster projection. But the more that we think about things, Schmidt’s return feels like a significant blow to Warren’s chances of pitching in October. Do the Yankees really need two long relievers capable of eating up innings if the starter leaves early?
We initially had veteran swingman Ryan Yarbrough in this spot, though he might have the advantage as a left-handed reliever.. He also has a 2.91 ERA in 21.2 second-half innings and has since recovered from a lingering right oblique problem.

item.title: [nytimes.com] The MLB prospects I was wrong about: Jacob Misiorowski, Ben Rice and more
